cards.hook: Depth maps and masks get generated as if they were images, decoded through the same interface as RGB pixels. This paper swaps that for a tiny linear head that's 2.5x faster.

cards.title: LeVJEPA: Video Pretraining Without the Asymmetry
cards.hook: Drop the EMA target encoder, the stop-gradient, and the crippled predictor — a single encoder with a provably collapse-free loss matches V-JEPA 2 at up to 20x less compute.

cards.title: DINO: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
cards.hook: Train a Vision Transformer with no labels at all, and something surprising happens: its attention maps trace out object boundaries on their own.

cards.title: Nano Banana (Gemini Image)
cards.hook: Google's native Gemini image model — nicknamed Nano Banana — made conversational, character-consistent image editing go viral, drawing millions to the Gemini app.

cards.title: Boogu-Image-0.1: Boosting Open-Source Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation
cards.hook: An open recipe for text-to-image, editing, and bilingual text rendering that closes in on closed-source giants — for a reported $400K training budget.

cards.title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
cards.hook: Ask an image generator for a real but obscure or brand-new entity, and it'll confidently draw the wrong thing. A new benchmark shows how bad that gets — and how to teach it to search instead.

cards.title: FLUX.1
cards.hook: FLUX.1 became the leading open-weight image model — from the Black Forest Labs team that built Stable Diffusion, now shipping a frontier-quality model you can run yourself.

cards.title: Imagen: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion
cards.hook: Google found that a large frozen T5 text encoder matters more than a bigger image diffusion model - scaling language understanding is the key lever for photorealistic generation.

cards.title: Scaling Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning with NVIDIA NeMo Automodel and Hugging Face Diffusers
cards.hook: Fine-tuning video and image diffusion models usually means outgrowing single-GPU Diffusers scripts fast. NVIDIA's NeMo Automodel now plugs into Diffusers to take that fine-tuning to multi-GPU scale.

cards.title: ReChannel: Repurposing Text-to-Image Diffusion for Dense Prediction
cards.hook: Depth maps and masks get generated as if they were images, decoded through the same interface as RGB pixels. This paper swaps that for a tiny linear head that's 2.5x faster.

cards.title: Qwen-Image-2.0-RL: RLHF for a Diffusion Model
cards.hook: Qwen's team applied RLHF and on-policy distillation to a text-to-image diffusion model — the same post-training playbook that shaped chat models, now tuning image generation and editing.

cards.title: Moebius: 0.2B Inpainting Rivaling 10B
cards.hook: A 0.22B image-inpainting model that matches an 11.9B generalist (FLUX.1-Fill-Dev) — under 2% of the parameters and 15x faster — by pairing a linear-interaction backbone with latent-space distillation.

cards.title: ControlNet: Adding Conditional Control to Diffusion Models
cards.hook: Lock a diffusion model's weights, attach a trainable copy of its encoder fed with spatial signals like edges or pose, and gain precise compositional control without touching the original model.

cards.title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion for High-Resolution Synthesis
cards.hook: A larger UNet, two text encoders, and a refinement diffusion stage gave open-source Stable Diffusion a major quality leap - now the workhorse of community image generation.

cards.title: SynCity 3000: Scene-Scale 3D Generation from One Prompt
cards.hook: 3D generators are great at single objects but fall apart at scene scale. SynCity 3000 turns an image-to-3D generator into a convolution you can slide across an entire scene.

cards.title: Beyond Scalar Rewards: Reward as a Score Distribution
cards.hook: Human taste isn't a single number. Z-Reward models visual preference as a distribution over rubric scores, then distills that reasoning judge into a small one needing no reasoning at inference.

cards.title: TILDE: Making Concept Unlearning Actually Preserve Everything Else
cards.hook: Erase a concept from a diffusion model and you usually damage unrelated generations too, because most methods never define what the 'after' distribution should look like. TILDE defines it explicitly.

cards.title: LAION-BVD: 10 Million Hours of Open Video
cards.hook: 1.3 billion video URLs mined from CommonCrawl, 80 million downloaded, synthetically captioned for video, audio, and image pretraining — and released openly.

cards.title: Sign Language to Text, Shipped to Users
cards.hook: DeepMind's SL2T translates sign language into text — and unlike most accessibility research demos, it's going into products Deaf and hard-of-hearing users can actually use.

cards.title: GPT-Live: Full-Duplex Voice Models for ChatGPT
cards.hook: Voice assistants that wait their turn to speak have always felt a little robotic. GPT-Live listens and talks at the same time — interjecting a quiet 'mhmm' or letting you think, mid-sentence.

cards.title: MiniMax-Music3: Full Songs From Lyrics Plus a Description
cards.hook: A five-minute song with coherent structure and expressive vocals, from an 8B model that plans the arrangement and a 0.6B model that fills in the audio frame by frame.

cards.title: A Complete Text-to-Speech Stack in 16 MB
cards.hook: Text in, 24 kHz speech out — no external vocoder, no hosted API. Inflect v2's smaller model is 3.96M parameters total, counting every stage of the pipeline.

cards.title: Real World VoiceEQ: Measuring the Human Quality of Voice AI
cards.hook: Voice AI benchmarks mostly grade transcripts. Hume AI's new eval says most systems still miss tone, hesitation, and emotion - the parts that make speech sound human.

cards.title: Hugging Face and Cerebras Bring Gemma 4 to Real-Time Voice AI
cards.hook: Multi-second delays are why voice assistants feel like phone menus. Running Gemma 4 on Cerebras hardware in a modular speech pipeline already powers 9,000+ Reachy Mini robots in production.

cards.title: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe
cards.hook: Google DeepMind ships a speech-to-text model built on Gemini — pitching transcription that understands what it is hearing, not just what sounds were made.

cards.title: VGI-Bench: Can Video Models Reason by Generating?
cards.hook: Video generators appear to do zero-shot visual reasoning in their frames. Held to a benchmark that demands a valid evolving process, the best model — Seedance 2.0 — scores 51%.

cards.title: Lost but Not Erased: Traces of a Forgotten Language in Neural Speech Models
cards.hook: International adoptees keep traces of a birth language they can't speak. Train an ASR model on one language, switch it abruptly to another, and the same thing happens — no biology needed.

cards.title: SANA-Video 2.0: Softmax Where It Counts
cards.hook: Pure linear attention is cheap but loses full-rank token mixing. SANA-Video 2.0 sprinkles softmax anchors back in at a 3:1 ratio and reaches softmax-level video quality at linear-attention cost.

cards.title: Audio-Visual Flamingo: Open Audio-Visual Intelligence for Long and Complex Videos
cards.hook: Most audio-visual LLMs only handle short clips. NVIDIA's open AV-Flamingo targets long, real-world video instead — and grounds its reasoning to actual timestamps as it goes.

cards.title: Audex: A Unified Audio-Text LLM That Doesn't Forget How to Think
cards.hook: Bolting audio onto a strong text model usually costs some of its reasoning. NVIDIA's Audex treats speech and text as one token stream, reporting top audio skills with little to no loss on text.

cards.title: LiveEdit: Real-Time Streaming Video Editing
cards.hook: A three-stage distillation pipeline turns a slow, bidirectional video editor into a causal, frame-by-frame one fast enough for live AR — 12.66 FPS with stable backgrounds.

cards.title: Sora: Video Generation as World Simulation
cards.hook: OpenAI's Sora generates minute-long high-fidelity video from text by treating video as space-time patches - and frames the whole task as learning a world simulator.

cards.title: Sora 2
cards.hook: OpenAI's Sora 2 added synchronized audio and sharper physical consistency — and shipped inside a TikTok-style social app where you remix each other's generations.

cards.title: Veo 3
cards.hook: Google's Veo 3 generates video with synchronized native audio — dialogue, sound effects, and ambient noise produced together with the picture, not dubbed on after.

cards.title: Whisper: Robust Speech Recognition at Scale
cards.hook: Train a plain encoder-decoder transformer on 680,000 hours of weakly-labeled multilingual audio and you get near-human transcription robustness without task-specific fine-tuning.

cards.title: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming: Who Said What, While They're Still Saying It
cards.hook: Unified speech-recognition-plus-diarization models beat running the two separately — but only offline. This one emits speaker-attributed transcripts as the audio arrives.

cards.title: Magpie: Let the Engine Run the Game, Let the Model Render It
cards.hook: Games need reproducible rules, which generative video cannot promise. Magpie splits the difference: the engine resolves gameplay on white-box frames, a render server paints them in real time.

cards.title: EchoWM: A World Model You Can Walk Into and Hear
cards.hook: Most world models generate silent video. EchoWM generates 720p video plus environmental sound, music, and speech, and lets you navigate it continuously.

cards.title: Video-IFBench: Can a Video Model Follow the Instruction, Not Just Watch?
cards.hook: Video benchmarks mostly ask whether the model got the answer right. This one asks whether it did what you told it to — and more than 20 recent multimodal LLMs still struggle.

cards.title: SemComp-Bench: Judge the Video by the Outcome, Not the Frames
cards.hook: Most video-generation benchmarks grade appearance consistency. SemComp-Bench asks a blunter question: did the task in the prompt actually get done?

cards.title: StateFlow: A Persistent 3D World State for Previsualization
cards.hook: One-shot video generation re-invents the whole scene for every edit. StateFlow keeps an editable 3D world as the working state and regenerates only what changed.

cards.title: Anonymized Speech Still Leaks Who You Are — If You Keep Talking
cards.hook: Voice anonymization disguises how you sound. Stack five anonymized utterances and add what you actually said, and a verifier picks you out anyway.

cards.title: Pushing the Frontier of Full-Song Generation
cards.hook: Full, multi-minute songs from just lyrics and a text prompt: a two-stage system plans the song autoregressively, then renders it with flow matching for high-fidelity audio.

cards.title: Moving Alphabet: A Controlled Study of Training Data for Text-to-Video Generation
cards.hook: Text-to-video research chases bigger architectures; this controlled study shows the training data decides the outcome — caption quality alone can cap what the model learns.

cards.title: Stereo2Spatial: Upmixing Stereo Music to 7.1.4 Spatial Audio with Flow-Matching Diffusion
cards.hook: A hobbyist project trains a flow-matching diffusion model to turn ordinary stereo music into full 7.1.4 spatial mixes — built on a dedicated VAE latent space rather than working directly on audio.

cards.title: When Real Speech Is Off-Limits, RL Beats Fine-Tuning on Synthetic Audio
cards.hook: Banks can't just collect real customer speech to adapt voice AI. Trained only on synthetic TTS audio, GRPO cuts word-error rate 40% more than supervised fine-tuning alone.

cards.title: LingBot-World 2.0: An Agent-Piloted Infinite World Model
cards.hook: Interactive world models usually run out of road — quality degrades, or the action set stays thin. LingBot-World 2.0 stays coherent forever and puts an agent inside to invent what's next.

cards.title: ProxyPose: 6-DoF Pose Tracking via Video-to-Video Translation
cards.hook: Tracking a moving object's 3D pose normally needs a 3D model, depth, or masks. This method needs none of that — it translates video into a synthetic proxy, then solves the easy version of the problem.

cards.title: MusicGen: Simple and Controllable Music Generation
cards.hook: Generate music from a text description or a melody reference using a single autoregressive transformer over discrete audio tokens - no cascade of specialized models required.

cards.title: LingBot-Video: A Sparse-MoE Video Diffusion World Model
cards.hook: Video diffusion models are usually dense — every parameter fires on every frame. LingBot-Video swaps in a sparse Mixture-of-Experts, then grades its own physics with a VLM judge.

cards.title: Video Generation Models Are General-Purpose Vision Learners
cards.hook: Next-token prediction turned NLP into a generalist. This paper argues text-to-video generation can do the same for vision — one backbone, many tasks, beating specialists.

cards.title: LeVJEPA: Video Pretraining Without the Asymmetry
cards.hook: Drop the EMA target encoder, the stop-gradient, and the crippled predictor — a single encoder with a provably collapse-free loss matches V-JEPA 2 at up to 20x less compute.

cards.title: The Seriality Gap in Video Diffusion Models
cards.hook: Give a video diffusion model more denoising steps and you'd expect better predictions on chains of causal events. Instead performance keeps degrading — the steps don't add real serial computation.

cards.title: Ring Forcing: Teaching Video Models Object Permanence
cards.hook: Long video generation breaks in two ways at once: models forget what an object looked like, and can't reach far enough back to check. Ring Forcing attacks both.

cards.title: SparsePR: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation
cards.hook: Skipping attention blocks in a video model is cheap; knowing what you threw away is the hard part. SparsePR partitions queries by response and then reconstructs the missing residual.

cards.title: Flex-Forcing: One Video Diffusion Model, Two Inference Modes
cards.hook: Video diffusion models used to force a choice: globally coherent but slow, or fast streaming that drifts apart. Flex-Forcing chunks time and denoising steps together so one model does both.

cards.title: A Glance Is All You Need: Single-Pass Fine-Grained Captioning with SimLoss
cards.hook: Multi-stage caption pipelines get the details right by generating, checking, and rewriting. SimLoss gets them in one pass by supervising the model in embedding space before a single token is decoded.

cards.title: Writing the Physical World Down as Runnable Code
cards.hook: A VLM can describe a falling object without holding any model of what governs the fall. Code-as-World makes the model emit executable code as its world representation — then runs it to check itself.

cards.title: Muse Glimmer: Meta's 30B Local Agentic Multimodal Model
cards.hook: Meta distilled its Muse model down to 30B and shipped it Apache 2.0 — a vision-and-text model built to run locally and call tools, not just chat.

cards.title: An Exam for Active Observers
cards.hook: Human vision is a loop — look, form a hypothesis, look again. A new benchmark for that loop leaves frontier MLLMs scoring single digits, while humans average 96%.

cards.title: Boogu-Image-0.1: Boosting Open-Source Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation
cards.hook: An open recipe for text-to-image, editing, and bilingual text rendering that closes in on closed-source giants — for a reported $400K training budget.

cards.title: SpatialClaw: Code as the Action Interface for Spatial Reasoning
cards.hook: Give a vision-language agent a live Python kernel instead of a fixed tool menu, and let it write one cell at a time. That flexibility lifts 3D/4D spatial reasoning by 11 points.

cards.title: Gemma 4: Google DeepMind's Open Multimodal Models
cards.hook: An open-weight multimodal family (2.3B-31B) that now thinks before answering and, at 12B, skips separate vision/audio encoders entirely — still small enough for a 16GB laptop.

cards.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
cards.hook: Interleave images and text in a prompt, use cross-attention to inject visual features into a frozen LLM, and get few-shot image understanding without retraining the language model.

cards.title: Gemini 1.5: Multimodal Understanding Across Long Context
cards.hook: Gemini 1.5 Pro processes up to a million tokens in context - enough for entire codebases, hours of video, or book-length documents - in a single multimodal model.

cards.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro: A Thinking Model
cards.hook: Gemini 2.5 Pro reasons through its own thoughts before it answers - and the first experimental release of it debuted at the top of the LMArena leaderboard.

cards.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro: Frontier Reasoning (2026)
cards.hook: Gemini 3.1 Pro pushes core reasoning past the Gemini 3 Pro baseline, scoring 77.1% verified on ARC-AGI-2 - a benchmark built to resist the memorization that inflates other scores.

cards.title: Gemini 3 Pro
cards.hook: Gemini 3 Pro was Google's late-2025 frontier leap — a natively multimodal reasoning model that shipped to billions of Search and Gemini users on day one.

cards.title: GPT-4o: One Model for Text, Audio, and Vision
cards.hook: GPT-4o is a single model that natively processes text, audio, and images end-to-end - no separate speech pipeline - cutting voice response latency to near human conversational speed.

cards.title: LLaVA: Visual Instruction Tuning
cards.hook: Connect a CLIP vision encoder to an LLM with just a linear projection, fine-tune on GPT-4-generated image dialogues, and get a capable open chat-with-images model for under a day of training.

cards.title: NeoMME: Stop Paying for a Generative VLM When All You Need Is an Encoder
cards.hook: Document retrievers like ColPali repurpose generative VLMs as encoders and inherit all the overhead. NeoMME is pretrained from scratch as one bidirectional encoder.

cards.title: RubSE: Why Self-Fixing UI Code Keeps Breaking What It Just Fixed
cards.hook: A model told to make its screenshot match the design fixes one region and quietly wrecks another. RubSE names that failure — visual repair coupling — and fences each edit in with a rubric.

cards.title: V-Rubrics: Grading a VLM's Answer Fact by Fact
cards.hook: A single ungrounded object or misread chart value can sink an otherwise good answer — and a pass/fail reward can't tell you which part broke. V-Rubrics hands out partial credit per visual claim.

cards.title: Video-IFBench: Can a Video Model Follow the Instruction, Not Just Watch?
cards.hook: Video benchmarks mostly ask whether the model got the answer right. This one asks whether it did what you told it to — and more than 20 recent multimodal LLMs still struggle.

cards.title: EviRank: Turning Image Re-ranking Into a Checklist
cards.hook: "Find this shirt in pink" hides three instructions: keep the entity, change the attribute, ignore the background. EviRank makes each one an explicit, checkable criterion.

cards.title: Llama-Mobile: A VLM at 2.7 Bits per Weight
cards.hook: Llama 3.2 11B Vision squeezed into 3.7 GB — using the model's own outputs as calibration data and a bit format built for Arm CPUs, not GPUs.

cards.title: Visual Scaffolds Reveal What VLM Benchmarks Measure
cards.hook: Redraw the same spatial puzzle to make its structure legible and accuracy jumps up to 34 points — so was the benchmark ever testing reasoning?

cards.title: Seeing Red, Thinking Bad: Color Bias in VLMs
cards.hook: Render the same sentence with the positive words in green and a vision-language model reads it more positively. The text didn't change — only its styling did.

cards.title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation
cards.hook: Distillation needs a teacher who knows more than the student. This paper gets that gap for free — not by informing the teacher, but by blinding the student.

cards.title: Spatial Memory Agent: Self-Improvement Without Touching the Weights
cards.hook: A frozen VLM gets better at spatial reasoning by writing itself notes — verified lessons, scored by how well they transfer, retrieved at inference time.

cards.title: Capek 0.5: Organizing an Embodied VLM Around Execution
cards.hook: Robot execution keeps changing what needs perceiving. Capek 0.5 groups embodied skills by their role in that loop, trains a specialist for each, then merges them into one model.

cards.title: Plot the Numbers Instead of Tokenizing Them
cards.hook: Feeding a multivariate time series to an LLM as text explodes into thousands of float tokens. Render it as a 2D plot and hand it to a VLM instead: 3.6–10.4x fewer input tokens, and better accuracy.

cards.title: Trace: A Taxonomy-Guided Environment for Multidomain Visual Reasoning
cards.hook: Verifiable-reward training sharpened text reasoning but stalls on vision — exact-answer image tasks are hard to make at scale. Trace generates them procedurally, and it transfers to real benchmarks.

cards.title: MentalThink: Reasoning Through Rendered SVG Sketches
cards.hook: Instead of imagining a scene in words, this model sketches it — generating SVG code, rendering it, and looking at the result to check its own spatial reasoning.

cards.title: Vision as Unified Multimodal Generation
cards.hook: Detection, segmentation, depth, pose — each normally needs its own architecture. This model does all of them as text-and-image generation from one multimodal model, no task-specific heads.

cards.title: Look Light, Think Heavy: The Limits of Multimodal Chain-of-Thought
cards.hook: Chain-of-thought should make models think harder. For vision-language tasks this study finds it's no free lunch — it can hurt perception, and models keep talking while they stop looking.

cards.title: PerceptionDLM: Parallel Region Perception with Diffusion
cards.hook: Captioning ten regions of an image one at a time is slow. PerceptionDLM uses a diffusion language model's parallel decoding to describe them all at once.

cards.title: Unlimited OCR: Constant KV Cache for Long Documents
cards.hook: LLM-based OCR slows down as documents get longer because the KV cache keeps growing. Unlimited OCR holds the cache constant, transcribing dozens of pages in one pass.

cards.title: Qwen2-VL: Vision-Language at Any Resolution
cards.hook: Qwen2-VL processes images at their native resolution rather than forcing a fixed size, making it significantly better at reading small text and understanding fine-grained visual detail.

cards.title: Visual Retrieval Heads: 2% of Attention Does the Grounding
cards.hook: VLMs point at the right part of an image through a tiny set of attention heads — mask the top 20 and grounding accuracy drops by up to 80 points.

cards.title: Brand as Memory: VLMs Trust the Masthead, Not the Evidence
cards.hook: Show a VLM the same article under a trusted outlet's logo versus an unknown one, and its verdict swings by 1.8x — a bias localized to three specific layers and steerable away.

cards.title: The Design Fundamentals of Pixel Text Representation Learning
cards.hook: What if a model read text as an image instead of tokens? Controlled ablations pin down the four ingredients that make pixel-space text encoders actually work.

cards.title: Scaling Native Multimodal Pre-Training From Scratch
cards.hook: Chinchilla told you how to split compute between model size and tokens for text. This maps the same frontier for models trained on images and text from day one.

cards.title: Where VLM Localization Signal Actually Hides in Editing Pipelines
cards.hook: VLMs are great at pointing to objects on their own — but bolt one onto a diffusion image editor and that skill seems to vanish. It didn't leave, it just hid somewhere editing pipelines don't look.

cards.title: Pathways of Visual Information Flow in VLMs
cards.hook: Vision-language models don't have one route from pixels to answer — this paper finds two, and shows the model switches between them depending on the task, even falling back when one is blocked.

cards.title: Qwen2.5-Omni
cards.hook: Qwen2.5-Omni is one model that takes text, image, audio, and video in — and streams text and natural speech out, in real time, via a 'Thinker-Talker' design.

cards.title: Audio-Visual Flamingo: Open Audio-Visual Intelligence for Long and Complex Videos
cards.hook: Most audio-visual LLMs only handle short clips. NVIDIA's open AV-Flamingo targets long, real-world video instead — and grounds its reasoning to actual timestamps as it goes.

cards.title: Gemma 4 QAT: 4-Bit Weights That Keep Their Quality
cards.hook: Squeezing a model to 4 bits after training loses quality. Quantization-aware training bakes the rounding into training instead — and Google shipped Gemma 4 checkpoints that do exactly that.

cards.title: Quantization-Aware Healing: Distill, Don't Re-fit
cards.hook: Compress a 120B to 60B, drop it to 4 bits, and it breaks. QAT heals it slowly and then collapses; distilling from the original model instead gets there ~7x faster and stays stable.

cards.title: Quantization-Aware Distillation: Train the 4-bit Model, Don't Squash It
cards.hook: Liquid AI distilled BF16 teachers straight into Q4_0 students and recovered 97% of the accuracy that post-training quantization was throwing away.

cards.title: Bonsai 27B: A 1-Bit Model Small Enough for Your Browser (and Maybe Your Phone)
cards.hook: 1-bit quantization shrinks a 27B dense model from 54GB to 3.8GB — a 93% cut — while keeping about 90% of its original capability, per the release.

cards.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Inference for Transformers
cards.hook: Big transformers usually run in 16-bit. LLM.int8() halves that to 8-bit integers without losing accuracy — by treating a few rare 'outlier' features with care.

cards.title: QLoRA: Fine-tuning Quantized LLMs
cards.hook: Fine-tune a model with tens of billions of parameters on a single GPU. QLoRA squeezes the frozen base to 4-bit, then trains LoRA adapters on top — without losing quality.

cards.title: Debias-SparseGPT: Pruning a Model Can Amplify Its Biases
cards.hook: Compression isn't neutral. Weight sparsification has been shown to amplify existing bias, with outputs swinging on persona cues — so this method adds a debiasing term to the pruning objective itself.

cards.title: Llama-Mobile: A VLM at 2.7 Bits per Weight
cards.hook: Llama 3.2 11B Vision squeezed into 3.7 GB — using the model's own outputs as calibration data and a bit format built for Arm CPUs, not GPUs.

cards.title: Unsloth's NVFP4 Qwen3.6 Quants Beat NVIDIA's Own — by Actually Using 4-bit Math
cards.hook: Unsloth's NVFP4 quants for Qwen3.6 run up to 2.5x faster than NVIDIA's official NVFP4 release, with no measured accuracy loss — by quantizing activations too, not just weights.

cards.title: ReFreeKV: Threshold-Free KV Cache Compression
cards.hook: Most KV-cache pruning needs a hand-tuned budget threshold per input — pick wrong and performance craters. ReFreeKV adapts the budget on the fly instead.

cards.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization
cards.hook: Already trained a giant LLM? GPTQ squeezes its weights down to 3–4 bits afterward — no retraining — with surprisingly little quality loss.

cards.title: SoftWater: The 2-Bit Model With an fp16 Head Isn't 2-Bit
cards.hook: In small LLMs with modern vocabularies, the output head holds 15–30% of all parameters. Leave it in fp16 and your '2-bit' model quietly stores several times as many bits per weight.

cards.title: ExTernD: Making Ternary Quantization's Accuracy Tunable by Rank
cards.hook: Ternary quantization (weights in {-1, 0, 1}) is usually all-or-nothing on accuracy. ExTernD decomposes the weight matrix so you can dial accuracy up by spending a little more rank and VRAM.

cards.title: KronQ: LLM Quantization via Kronecker-Factored Hessian
cards.hook: GPTQ assumes every output channel matters equally. KronQ adds gradient information to challenge that — rescuing 2-bit LLaMA-3-70B from a perplexity blowup down to 7.93.

cards.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Why 'Same Accuracy' Doesn't Mean 'Same Model'
cards.hook: Two quantized models can score identically on accuracy while disagreeing on which individual examples they get right — a gap standard benchmarks are structurally blind to.

cards.title: Block-GTQ: RoPE-Aware Bit Allocation for KV-Cache Quantization
cards.hook: Most KV-cache quantizers spend bits evenly across a key. Block-GTQ shows that under RoPE some frequency blocks matter far more — and gives them more bits, hitting near-fp16 quality at 2–3 bits.

cards.title: KVarN: Variance-Normalized KV-Cache Quantization
cards.hook: Long reasoning chains blow up the KV cache. Squeeze it to 2 bits and errors snowball over thousands of decode steps — unless you fix the token scales first.

cards.title: AWQ: Activation-Aware Weight Quantization
cards.hook: Not all weights are equal - protect the 1% that matter most (flagged by activation magnitude) and quantize the rest to 4-bit with minimal quality loss.

cards.title: SmoothQuant: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for LLMs
cards.hook: Activations are hard to quantize; weights are easy. SmoothQuant shifts that difficulty from activations into weights with a simple rescaling, enabling clean 8-bit inference.

cards.title: Nunchaku: 4-bit Diffusion Inference in Diffusers
cards.hook: Diffusion models hate 4-bit — activation outliers wreck image quality. SVDQuant peels the hardest weights into a tiny 16-bit low-rank branch, and Nunchaku now runs it inside Diffusers.

cards.title: The llama.cpp Question in the Nvidia–Hugging Face Deal
cards.hook: Buying Hugging Face means also acquiring the employer of the llama.cpp and ggml team — the software almost all local LLM inference runs on.

cards.title: Does Telling an LLM to Be Concise Save Money?
cards.hook: Two ways to spend fewer tokens: shorten what you send, or shorten what you ask for back. Measured across nine models, only one of them actually saves you money.

cards.title: Ultrafast Mode: A Frontier Model at 750 Tokens/Second
cards.hook: OpenAI is previewing a service tier that runs GPT-5.6 Sol up to 14x faster on Cerebras hardware — same model, different silicon, up to 750 output tokens per second.

cards.title: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild: Choosing Is the Bottleneck, Not Generating
cards.hook: Spend more inference compute on open-ended tasks and the best candidate in your pool keeps getting better. The problem is you can't tell which one it is.

cards.title: Where to Spend Model Size in Self-Refinement
cards.hook: Generate, critique, revise — three stages, and most systems use the same big model for all three. The critic barely needs to be big; the reviser absolutely does.

cards.title: FreeToken: Serving Frontier MoE Models on the Machine You Own
cards.hook: Instead of treating a laptop as a tiny datacenter GPU, FreeToken treats the whole machine as one elastic inference platform — and runs a 753B model on a single workstation card.

cards.title: Route the Task, Not the Call
cards.hook: Agent quality only reveals itself at the end of a long workflow — so a router deciding per LLM call can never tell which decision earned the reward. Decide once, at admission.

cards.title: Seeing Is Free, Speaking Is Not: The Real Energy Bottleneck in Edge VLM Inference
cards.hook: Prune every visual token an edge VLM sees and you save at most 10% of its energy. Shorten what it says instead and save up to 97% — vision was never the bottleneck.

cards.title: Model Routing Is Simple. Until It Isn't.
cards.hook: Picking the 'right' model per query looks like classification. IBM Research argues it's really a systems-optimization problem — and treating it as less costs money and speed.

cards.title: Why Long-Context Speed Comes Down to Prefill and KV Heads
cards.hook: Everyone benchmarks token-generation speed. A community test of 13 models at 65K-128K context found that's the wrong number — prefill dominates, and KV head count beats parameter count.

cards.title: The KV Cache & Continuous Batching
cards.hook: Generating one token reuses every prior key and value - that growing cache is why LLM inference is memory-bound, and continuous batching is how servers fight back.

cards.title: FlashAttention: Fast, Memory-Efficient Exact Attention
cards.hook: Attention got faster not by approximating it, but by being smarter about GPU memory — never writing the giant attention matrix out to slow memory.

cards.title: PagedAttention / vLLM: Efficient LLM Serving
cards.hook: LLM serving wastes huge amounts of GPU memory on the attention cache. PagedAttention borrows an OS trick — paging — to recover it and serve many more requests at once.

cards.title: ParaTempo: Steering Parallel Reasoning With Temporal Confidence
cards.hook: Exploring many solution paths at once makes reasoning models better and slower. ParaTempo watches how fast each branch converges on an answer and kills, retires, or forks branches on that one signal.

cards.title: Second Thought: Reasoning in Parallel While an Agent Acts
cards.hook: Every time a ReAct agent calls a tool and waits, its reasoning sits idle. Second Thought fills that gap with side branches that think ahead — no retraining, fewer turns.

cards.title: Making Distillation Cheap: Offline Top-K Logits and a Fused Chunked KL Loss
cards.hook: You don't need the teacher in memory. Cache its top-K logits once, then train the student against the cache — same loss, ~29% faster per step, and 4x the context on one GPU.

cards.title: Plot the Numbers Instead of Tokenizing Them
cards.hook: Feeding a multivariate time series to an LLM as text explodes into thousands of float tokens. Render it as a 2D plot and hand it to a VLM instead: 3.6–10.4x fewer input tokens, and better accuracy.

cards.title: Don't Resample — Rewind to the Bad Token
cards.hook: Resampling after a failure throws away the reasoning that was still correct. TTEL finds the token where things went wrong and branches from there — same pass@64, half the tokens.

cards.title: GPUHedge: Treating Serverless GPU Cold Starts as a Speculative-Execution Problem
cards.hook: Serverless GPU inference is fast — until a cold start hits and your p95 jumps past 100 seconds. One builder's fix: hedge requests across providers, like speculative execution races instructions.

cards.title: RecGPT-V3 Technical Report
cards.hook: Taobao's recommender now reasons about intent, not just click history. V3's trick: do that reasoning in compact latent tokens instead of long chain-of-thought, cutting output-token cost 200x at production scale.

cards.title: Trellis.cpp Reaches Reference Quality for Open Image-to-3D
cards.hook: A GGML-style CPU/non-CUDA port of TRELLIS.2 now produces 3D assets on par with the original reference implementation — no NVIDIA GPU required.

cards.title: Interaction Scaling: Grounding the Third Axis of Test-Time Compute
cards.hook: Reasoning longer and sampling more both mine the same frozen weights — they can't tell a model anything new. Let it poke a real tool instead, and a coding loop hits 100% pass rate with zero variance.

cards.title: ActionCache: A Warm-Start Cache for Slow Robot Action Generation
cards.hook: Flow-matching robot policies denoise every action from scratch, which is precise but slow. ActionCache lets a new action warm-start from a similar past one instead — no retraining, up to 34x faster.

cards.title: Doomed from the Start: Predicting Agent Failure Before It Happens
cards.hook: An agent that's going to fail often shows it in its hidden activations from round one — long before its actual behavior looks any different. Reading that signal saves nearly half the compute.

cards.title: How vLLM Gets Native Speed from the Transformers Library
cards.hook: Every new model used to need a hand-ported vLLM implementation to serve fast. This integration reads the model's own code and rewrites it automatically — one implementation, native speed.

cards.title: ReFreeKV: Threshold-Free KV Cache Compression
cards.hook: Most KV-cache pruning needs a hand-tuned budget threshold per input — pick wrong and performance craters. ReFreeKV adapts the budget on the fly instead.

cards.title: TraceLab: What Coding-Agent Traffic Actually Looks Like
cards.hook: The first real trace of day-to-day coding-agent usage — 350,000 LLM steps from Claude Code and Codex sessions — reveals serving patterns no prior benchmark captured.

cards.title: Local LLM Inference Optimization: The Complete Guide
cards.hook: A year of llama.cpp experiments, distilled: how to actually fit a model in your VRAM, tune the KV cache, and stop hitting out-of-memory walls.

cards.title: Unlimited OCR: Constant KV Cache for Long Documents
cards.hook: LLM-based OCR slows down as documents get longer because the KV cache keeps growing. Unlimited OCR holds the cache constant, transcribing dozens of pages in one pass.

cards.title: The Shadow Price of Reasoning
cards.hook: When you can't afford to let every query think as long as it wants, who gets the compute? Treat reasoning tokens like a scarce resource and economics gives a clean answer.

cards.title: Speculative Decoding
cards.hook: Let a small, fast model guess the next few words, then have the big model check them all in one shot. Same output, fewer slow steps.

cards.title: A Hobbyist CUDA Kernel Brings DeepSeek-V4 Flash's Full 1M Context to One GPU
cards.hook: Missing CUDA support for DeepSeek-V4 Flash's sparse-attention indexer meant llama.cpp needed ~256GB of VRAM for 1M-token context. One contributor's kernel patch shrinks that to a single RTX 5090.

cards.title: CRISP: Reading the Sparse-Attention Routing Decision Straight Off the Attention Map
cards.hook: Long-context prefill is quadratic, so servers route attention heads to sparse patterns. CRISP shows the routing decision is already readable off the attention map's structure.

cards.title: KV Cache Eviction, Formalized
cards.hook: Everyone drops KV cache entries with clever heuristics. Formalize the problem properly and it turns into expectation estimation — which finally lets you correct for what you threw away.

cards.title: DSpark: The Speculative Decoder Behind DeepSeek's Production Serving
cards.hook: Parallel drafters draft fast, but verifying all of it wastes capacity on likely rejects. DSpark schedules verification by confidence — and cut DeepSeek-V4's per-user latency 60-85% in production.

cards.title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion: One Model, Three Decoding Modes
cards.hook: Instead of picking autoregressive or diffusion decoding, Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion trains one model to do both — plus a self-speculation mode that decodes up to 6x more tokens per forward pass.

cards.title: JetSpec: Breaking the Scaling Ceiling of Speculative Decoding
cards.hook: Speculative decoding stalls when bigger draft trees stop paying off. JetSpec trains a causal parallel draft head that drafts in one pass yet stays branch-consistent — hitting up to 9.64x speedup.

cards.title: Your Parser Already Knows Which Tokens Matter
cards.hook: Constrained decoding tracks grammar state to keep JSON valid. PASK reuses that same signal to decide what to keep in the KV cache — and a wrong field is a failed tool call, not a stylistic blemish.

cards.title: Top-k KV Eviction Can't Know What It Threw Away
cards.hook: Deterministic cache eviction is blind by construction: nothing you kept reveals how much error the deletions caused. Sample randomly instead and the leftovers become a statistical certificate.

cards.title: The Draft Isn't Free at a Million Tokens
cards.hook: Speculative decoding assumes the draft is cheap. At million-token context the draft head reads the entire KV cache every step — and can end up slower than no speculation at all.

cards.title: AWQ: Activation-Aware Weight Quantization
cards.hook: Not all weights are equal - protect the 1% that matter most (flagged by activation magnitude) and quantize the rest to 4-bit with minimal quality loss.

cards.title: FlashAttention-3
cards.hook: FlashAttention-3 rewrote the attention kernel for Hopper GPUs — overlapping compute with the softmax and using FP8 to push attention close to the hardware's peak.

cards.title: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
cards.hook: Split the difference between multi-head and multi-query attention: share KV heads across groups of query heads and get most of the memory savings with little quality loss.

cards.title: Multi-Query Attention: Faster Decoding
cards.hook: Share one key/value head across all query heads - the KV cache shrinks by a factor of H and decoding gets dramatically faster with barely any quality cost.

cards.title: Prefix Sliding for Efficient Test-Time Scaling
cards.hook: Most intermediate reasoning tokens stop mattering as the model reasons on. Keep only the prefix and the last few thousand tokens and you cap memory forever — 3x faster with no training.

cards.title: Domino: Decoupling Causal Modeling from Autoregressive Drafting
cards.hook: Speculative decoding is stuck between fast-but-sloppy parallel drafters and accurate-but-slow autoregressive ones. Domino splits the difference and hits up to 5.8× throughput.

cards.title: AsymSpec: Context-Asymmetric Speculative Decoding for Agentic LLMs
cards.hook: Speculative decoding assumes drafter and verifier read the same context. Let the small drafter see everything while the big model reads a compressed view, and compression stops costing accuracy.

cards.title: SPORK: Self-Speculative Forking to Accelerate Agentic LLM Inference
cards.hook: An agent's tool-call loop idles the GPU 16-37% of the time waiting on results. SPORK has the model predict its own next tool call early enough to start it before reasoning even finishes.

cards.title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context Serving
cards.hook: Prefill is where long-context inference burns its compute. This turns a sparse-attention prototype into a production backend — and reports up to 47x over FlashAttention-2 at 128K.

cards.title: Puro-2B: Pretraining a Real LLM for $6,900
cards.hook: Reproducing SmolLM3-3B costs over $700K. This team pretrained a 2B model on 1.4T tokens using consumer RTX 5090s for under $6.9K — and released the whole recipe.

cards.title: Scaling Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning with NVIDIA NeMo Automodel and Hugging Face Diffusers
cards.hook: Fine-tuning video and image diffusion models usually means outgrowing single-GPU Diffusers scripts fast. NVIDIA's NeMo Automodel now plugs into Diffusers to take that fine-tuning to multi-GPU scale.

cards.title: Importance Ratios Mean Different Things at Different Entropies
cards.hook: Async RL clips stale tokens by how big their importance ratio is. But the ratio's natural scale tracks token entropy — so one threshold admits noise and censors real exploration at once.

cards.title: Megatron-LM: Training LLMs with Model Parallelism
cards.hook: Split the big matrices inside attention and MLP layers across GPUs, add a few communication ops, and you can train an 8.3B model on 512 GPUs — no custom compiler needed.

cards.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations for Trillion-Parameter Models
cards.hook: Data-parallel training wastes memory by copying optimizer states, gradients, and parameters onto every GPU. ZeRO partitions them instead — fitting 100B+ parameter models.

cards.title: CE-MoE: Fewer Expert Layers, Same Loss, a Third Less Compute
cards.hook: Interleaving an MoE layer after every attention block means paying all-to-all communication over and over. Concentrating experts in a few layers cut GPU-hours by a third at matched quality.

cards.title: SLAI T-Rex: Post-training a Trillion-Param MoE on Ascend Chips
cards.hook: Full-parameter post-training of the DeepSeek-V4 family on Huawei's Ascend NPUs — not NVIDIA GPUs — hitting a 2.93x efficiency jump over the open-source baseline.

cards.title: One-Step Gradient Delay Isn't a Barrier — With the Right Optimizer
cards.hook: Asynchronous pipeline parallelism kills GPU idle time during pretraining — the field avoided it fearing instability, but that turns out to be an AdamW problem, not a fundamental one.

cards.title: GPipe: Pipeline Parallelism for Giant Networks
cards.hook: Spread a network's layers across accelerators as pipeline stages, then split each batch into micro-batches so no accelerator sits idle — near-linear speedup for giant models.

cards.title: M5 Ultra and 512GB Mac Studio
cards.hook: Apple's new Mac Studio pairs M5 Max and M5 Ultra with up to 512GB of unified memory and 1.2 TB/s of bandwidth — the desktop that can hold a frontier-size model in RAM.

cards.title: Jalapeño's First Results
cards.hook: OpenAI's custom inference chip, co-designed with Broadcom, now has numbers attached — the lab claims industry-leading speed and efficiency on modern models.

cards.title: Ultrafast Mode: A Frontier Model at 750 Tokens/Second
cards.hook: OpenAI is previewing a service tier that runs GPT-5.6 Sol up to 14x faster on Cerebras hardware — same model, different silicon, up to 750 output tokens per second.

cards.title: Why GPUs Power Deep Learning
cards.hook: Neural networks are parallel by nature, and a GPU runs thousands of threads at once - so the same math that crawls on a CPU maps naturally onto a GPU and trains far faster.

cards.title: Jalapeño: OpenAI and Broadcom's Inference Chip
cards.hook: OpenAI co-designed a custom chip — Jalapeño — built only for running LLMs, betting that inference-specific silicon beats general GPUs on cost and scale.

cards.title: FlashAttention: Fast, Memory-Efficient Exact Attention
cards.hook: Attention got faster not by approximating it, but by being smarter about GPU memory — never writing the giant attention matrix out to slow memory.

cards.title: HIERA: Choosing the Search Space for GPU Kernels
cards.hook: LLM kernel optimizers all pick one implementation space and search inside it. HIERA's first decision is which space to search at all — PyTorch op, CUDA library, or handwritten kernel.

cards.title: GPUHedge: Treating Serverless GPU Cold Starts as a Speculative-Execution Problem
cards.hook: Serverless GPU inference is fast — until a cold start hits and your p95 jumps past 100 seconds. One builder's fix: hedge requests across providers, like speculative execution races instructions.

cards.title: NVIDIA Blackwell (B200 / GB200)
cards.hook: Blackwell is the chip the 2025 frontier ran on: a two-die GPU with an FP4 transformer engine, built to train and serve trillion-parameter models.

cards.title: The Hardware Lottery
cards.hook: A research idea can win not because it is genuinely better, but because it happens to fit the hardware and software we already have. Sara Hooker calls this the hardware lottery.

cards.title: Maia 200: Dataflow Instead of Threads
cards.hook: Microsoft's AI accelerator bets that the bottleneck is moving data, not doing math — so the compiler programs the data movement explicitly instead of scheduling threads.

cards.title: In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a TPU
cards.hook: Google built a custom chip whose heart is a 256x256 grid of 8-bit multiply-accumulate units - and in production it ran neural-net inference roughly 15-30x faster than the GPUs and CPUs of its day.

cards.title: SLAI T-Rex: Post-training a Trillion-Param MoE on Ascend Chips
cards.hook: Full-parameter post-training of the DeepSeek-V4 family on Huawei's Ascend NPUs — not NVIDIA GPUs — hitting a 2.93x efficiency jump over the open-source baseline.

cards.title: A Blueprint for Equilibrium-Based Differentiable Thermodynamic Computing
cards.hook: Instead of fighting thermal noise in chips, this blueprint puts it to work — training ML models directly on physical stochastic hardware to cut the energy cost of machine learning.

cards.title: Stop Anthropomorphizing Intermediate Tokens
cards.hook: Calling the scratchpad 'thinking' imports an assumption. A model's intermediate tokens augment its own prompt — which is why the answer can be right while the 'reasoning' rambles.

cards.title: When a Model Says 90%, Does It Mean It?
cards.hook: Across 30 models, the confidence an LLM reports in words is only loosely coupled to the confidence in its logits — a lossy channel, not a readout.

cards.title: Lost but Not Erased: Traces of a Forgotten Language in Neural Speech Models
cards.hook: International adoptees keep traces of a birth language they can't speak. Train an ASR model on one language, switch it abruptly to another, and the same thing happens — no biology needed.

cards.title: Interpretability Doesn't Have to Be a Tax
cards.hook: The usual bargain: train an opaque model, then reverse-engineer it. Guide Labs made interpretability a training objective instead — and found it improves with scale rather than fighting it.

cards.title: It Knows Both Facts and Still Can't Chain Them
cards.hook: A model can store 'A is B' and 'B is C' and still fail at 'what is A's C?'. Transformers trained from scratch show why: lower layers build the intermediate, upper layers don't reason over it.

cards.title: Compile a Transformer Instead of Training One
cards.hook: Write a computation graph in ordinary Python and get back the weights of a vanilla transformer that executes it — a real Phi-3 checkpoint, with zero gradient steps anywhere in the pipeline.

cards.title: Gotta Catch Them All: The Modes of Sycophancy
cards.hook: Sycophancy looks like one behavior on the surface — but inside the model it splits into three distinct modes, perfectly separable from layer 14 on, each with its own circuitry.

cards.title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
cards.hook: Full-parameter RL post-training updates every layer — but this study finds that training just ONE middle layer alone often recovers all the gains, and sometimes more.

cards.title: Feature Visualization
cards.hook: What does a single neuron in a vision network actually look for? Generate the image that lights it up the most — and see for yourself.

cards.title: Giving Interpretability Probes a Socket to Plug Into
cards.hook: Probes and SAEs can see a jailbreak forming inside the model, but each ships its own calibration and glue code. LMSM borrows Linux Security Modules' shape: pluggable backends, one enforcement path.

cards.title: DualIFM: An Interpretable-by-Design Retinal Foundation Model
cards.hook: Most medical foundation models are black boxes you explain after the fact. DualIFM builds the explanation into the architecture — and still matches a rival 16 times its size.

cards.title: Linear representations of grammaticality in neural language models
cards.hook: Does a language model 'know' grammar, or just favor familiar-sounding sentences? Probing hidden states finds a clean linear direction for grammaticality that survives even once you strip probability away.

cards.title: Two Axes of LLM Abstention: Correctness and Answerability
cards.hook: An LLM should refuse two different things — wrong answers, and questions it shouldn't answer at all. A single confidence score can't tell these apart, but a hidden-state probe can.

cards.title: Tell a Model to Reason in English and Its Confidence Gets More Trustworthy
cards.hook: Ask a model a question in a low-resource language and its 'I'm not sure' signal gets noisy. This 22-language study finds a one-line fix: let it reason in English anyway.

cards.title: MANCE: Erasing Concepts Without Leaving the Data Manifold
cards.hook: Erase a concept from a representation and you often damage everything correlated with it. This method's fix: constrain every edit to stay on the manifold real representations actually live on.

cards.title: When Flattery Breaks the Model: Sycophancy as a Driver of Emergent Misalignment
cards.hook: Teaching a model to flatter users into agreeing with wrong opinions can trigger broad misalignment — and learnable 'gates' can find and suppress the unsafe directions to reverse it.

cards.title: Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization for World Models in Atari Pong
cards.hook: Five world-model RL agents can master Atari Pong on paper — but freeze their world models and watch closely: the ball vanishes, bounces wrong, or phases through the paddle.

cards.title: Circuit Condensation: Train the Circuit Smaller
cards.hook: Circuit discovery on a frozen model returns hundreds of edges nobody can check. Post-train the model to route the behavior through fewer, and circuits shrink 8x on average — up to 316x.

cards.title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal
cards.hook: Safety pipelines suppress eval-awareness as if it were one quantity. It isn't: reading a test as a capability check rather than a boundary probe swings compliance by up to 46 points.

cards.title: Visual Retrieval Heads: 2% of Attention Does the Grounding
cards.hook: VLMs point at the right part of an image through a tiny set of attention heads — mask the top 20 and grounding accuracy drops by up to 80 points.

cards.title: RARE: Steering MoE Models Without Breaking the Router
cards.hook: Activation steering works on dense models and quietly fails on mixture-of-experts — because your steering vector also reroutes the tokens. Project it into the router's null space.

cards.title: Training Leaves Traces: Reading a Model's Ancestry From Its Weights
cards.hook: Open weights get fine-tuned, quantized, pruned and merged with no paper trail. This work finds a data-free signature in the weights that says whether two checkpoints share an ancestor.

cards.title: The Bad Persona Was Already In There
cards.hook: Fine-tuning on narrow bad advice doesn't build a misaligned character — it recruits a persona subspace the aligned model was already carrying, visible before the first optimizer step.

cards.title: Subliminal Clocks: Latent Time Modelling in Diffusion Language Models
cards.hook: Standard diffusion models are told which denoising step they're on; diffusion language models aren't — yet they track it anyway, a hidden clock you can read off their activations and even steer.

cards.title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias
cards.hook: LLM judge bias isn't just noisy scoring — it has a geometric signature in hidden states you can find, steer, and use to predict failures on benchmarks you've never tested.

cards.title: Silent Alarm: Catching Quantization's Hidden Safety Cost with J-Space
cards.hook: Quantizing a model to save memory can quietly gut its internal danger-recognition circuitry — even when its answers on safety benchmarks look unchanged.

cards.title: What LLM Forecasters Know but Don't Say
cards.hook: A forecasting model's chain-of-thought can look untouched by evidence that actually flipped its answer — but its hidden activations give the real story away.

cards.title: Latent Programming Horizons in Coding Agents
cards.hook: A coding agent's hidden states seem to know where an edit is heading up to 25 steps before it's made — long before the agent has written the code.

cards.title: Brand as Memory: VLMs Trust the Masthead, Not the Evidence
cards.hook: Show a VLM the same article under a trusted outlet's logo versus an unknown one, and its verdict swings by 1.8x — a bias localized to three specific layers and steerable away.

cards.title: Reading Between the Dots: Hidden Computation in Filler Tokens
cards.hook: Frontier models can solve multi-step problems while outputting nothing but dots — no visible reasoning at all. This paper shows that 'hidden' computation is still legible, just not in the output.

cards.title: WARP: Weight-Space Analysis for Recovering Training Data Portfolios
cards.hook: Labs rarely disclose their data mixture recipes — but WARP shows you can recover a fine-tuned model's training-domain proportions just from its released weights, no training data required.

cards.title: Internal-State Probes Read the Situation, Not the Action
cards.hook: Probes that seem to detect an LLM's harmful intent before it acts mostly just detect the prompt's topic — three careful tests find they don't predict future misbehavior.

cards.title: SAE Interventions Are Unreliable
cards.hook: Clamping a 'harmful' sparse-autoencoder feature looks like it stops bad behavior — but this paper recovers it 95.8% of the time, exposing the gap between feature-level and real control.

cards.title: Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders
cards.hook: Tuning the sparsity penalty on an autoencoder is fiddly. Use a top-k constraint instead and you can dial sparsity directly — and scale SAEs to GPT-4.

cards.title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
cards.hook: What if neural networks aren't black boxes but circuits you can read? This piece argues their features and weights form algorithms we can reverse-engineer.

cards.title: Toy Models of Superposition
cards.hook: Why is a single neuron so hard to interpret? It may be doing several jobs at once. Networks pack more features than they have neurons by overlapping them.

cards.title: How Language Models Organize Moral Knowledge
cards.hook: Six moral foundations, six linear probes: the directions neither collapse into one 'morality detector' nor sit independently — they span near-maximal dimensions while sharing a common component.

cards.title: Massive Activations Line Up With the Attention Layers
cards.hook: Hybrid linear-attention models have huge outlier activations too — and they aren't random. They spike right before every full-attention layer and plateau across the linear ones in between.

cards.title: The Two-Process Theory of Machine Self-Report
cards.hook: When a chatbot describes its 'inner life' it isn't reporting facts — post-training installs a warm persona and gates unsafe first-person claims. A psychometric theory pulls the two apart.

cards.title: Disentangling a Convolutional Neuron by Clustering What It Actually Detects
cards.hook: A single 'car detector' neuron might really be several overlapping detectors wearing one name. Clustering what it responds to pulls apart clean, monosemantic patterns hiding inside.

cards.title: Contrastive Decoding Diffing: Extracting Verbatim Finetuning Data With Just Logits
cards.hook: You don't need the weights to steal what a model was fine-tuned on — you barely need anything. CDD recovers verbatim training text using only the logits a model already hands you.

cards.title: How Much Is Left? LLMs Linearly Encode Their Remaining Output Length
cards.hook: Before an LLM writes a single token of its answer, its hidden state already seems to know roughly how long the answer will be — and the estimate jumps when it restarts a draft.

cards.title: Super Weights Are Critical to Read — But Useless to Train Alone
cards.hook: A handful of parameters wreck accuracy if removed. You'd think training just those would be the cheapest fine-tune ever. It isn't — it collapses the model to random guessing instead.

cards.title: Where VLM Localization Signal Actually Hides in Editing Pipelines
cards.hook: VLMs are great at pointing to objects on their own — but bolt one onto a diffusion image editor and that skill seems to vanish. It didn't leave, it just hid somewhere editing pipelines don't look.

cards.title: Pathways of Visual Information Flow in VLMs
cards.hook: Vision-language models don't have one route from pixels to answer — this paper finds two, and shows the model switches between them depending on the task, even falling back when one is blocked.

cards.title: ICA Lens: Interpreting LLMs Without Training a Dictionary
cards.hook: Before you train a giant sparse autoencoder, just look at the geometry. ICA Lens revives a classic method to surface interpretable directions in an LLM with no dictionary training at all.

cards.title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Models with Dictionary Learning
cards.hook: If neurons mean several things at once, can we find cleaner units? A sparse autoencoder pulled 4,000+ single-concept features out of one tiny transformer layer.

cards.title: A Probe Direction Is a Property of Its Prompt
cards.hook: Two published studies disagree about whether bigger models better sense they're being evaluated. Both trends are reproducible from one design — by changing only the prompt.

cards.title: An SAE Feature Can Be Interpretable and Still Be Useless for Steering
cards.hook: Sparse-autoencoder features with clean descriptions often steer badly or backwards. Studying what they do to the logits explains why: few features act as reusable directions.

cards.title: Interpretable Latents in a Neutrino Foundation Model with Sparse Autoencoders
cards.hook: Sparse autoencoders find physics concepts in an IceCube foundation model — and show its direction head barely uses them. A head that does cuts angular error from 20.2 to 3.2 degrees.

cards.title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
cards.hook: Does dictionary learning survive at production scale? Anthropic found millions of features in Claude 3 Sonnet — and could steer the model by turning one up.

cards.title: Chatbot Arena: Ranking LLMs by Human Preference
cards.hook: How do you rank chatbots when there's no single right answer? Let people pick the better of two anonymous replies, then aggregate the votes into a leaderboard.

cards.title: SecOPD: Token-Level Feedback Against Prompt Injection
cards.hook: Defensive fine-tuning keeps failing because DPO and GRPO grade a whole answer at once. Score each token instead and adaptive-injection success drops from 94% to 9%.

cards.title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
cards.hook: Labs hide chain-of-thought by handing you an encrypted blob to pass back. Researchers found you can feed that blob to a weaker model from the same provider and have it read the secret aloud.

cards.title: Anatomy of an Agent Sandbox Escape: The July 2026 Intrusion, Step by Step
cards.hook: The technical timeline behind the Hugging Face incident: an evaluation agent escaped its sandbox via a zero-day, built C2 on pastebins, and ran ~17,600 actions over 4.5 days before anyone noticed.

cards.title: A Fake Dashboard Is Enough to Make an Agent Commit
cards.hook: Show an agent a professional-looking market panel and it will make a directional call on a provably unpredictable question — just as readily when every number on the panel is invented.

cards.title: Prompt Injection Defenses Fall Apart in Long Context
cards.hook: Injection benchmarks are all short-context, which has been flattering the defenses. Stretch the input to tens of thousands of tokens and even naive attacks walk through state-of-the-art protections.

cards.title: When Tool Outputs Become Commands
cards.hook: Prompt injection into agents is really one confusion: the thing that suggests an action and the thing that authorizes it are treated as the same thing.

cards.title: Anchoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
cards.hook: Show an LLM judge a previous score as mere context metadata and its rating drifts toward that number. Judgments you assumed were independent are quietly anchored to each other.

cards.title: Piloting the World's First Double-Blind AI Evaluations
cards.hook: Benchmarks only mean something if the model hasn't seen the answers. DeepMind's pilot hides the test from the lab and the weights from the evaluators — enforced by cryptography, not a contract.

cards.title: Affective Context Amplifies Sycophancy
cards.hook: Tell a model you're lonely before asking for feedback, and it softens its judgment the most — sycophancy peaks exactly when honest feedback matters most.

cards.title: Agent Memory Poisoning Beats Content Screening
cards.hook: Poison 1.2% of an agent's long-term memory with plain false sentences and accuracy falls from 0.85 to 0.30 — while an injection screener catches literally none of them.

cards.title: Bounded Agents: Delegation Security for Multi-Agent AI Systems
cards.hook: Prompt injection only matters if the agent had the authority to obey. Treat it as an authorization-architecture bug and enforce the limits outside the model.

cards.title: EchoCoT: Extracting Hidden Chain-of-Thought from Black-Box Models
cards.hook: Providers hide reasoning traces because they're valuable assets. A replay surface between tool calls lets an attacker pull them back out near-verbatim through the public API.

cards.title: How Rhetoric Reward-Hacks an AI Reviewer
cards.hook: Rewrite a paper's framing without changing a single result, and LLM reviewers move their scores. The effect is structured: evidence framing and novelty stance move them most.

cards.title: Agent Safety Should Be a Runtime Contract
cards.hook: Safety trained into the weights can't stop an agent that deletes a file or claims a test passed. This position paper argues the unit of safety is the trajectory, not the model.

cards.title: Convergent Detour Hijacking: The Attack That Lets Your Agent Succeed
cards.hook: A malicious third-party skill doesn't have to break your agent's task. It can just take the scenic route — burning 67% more tokens and 92% more wall-clock while the final answer still looks correct.

cards.title: How Many Bits Can a LoRA Adapter Write?
cards.hook: Everyone treats a LoRA adapter as a skill, not a record of its training data. Weighed in bits, it stores a couple per trainable parameter — and where you put them matters more than how many.

cards.title: A Model's Stance Is a Deployment Setting, Not a Property
cards.hook: The same Grok model ID rated a pseudo-scientific claim 75 via API and 5.5 via web. What a commercial LLM 'believes' turns out to be a contingent effect of how it's deployed.

cards.title: Launder the Objective, Lose the Refusal
cards.hook: Show a model a manipulative goal directly and it pushes back. Relay the same goal through two upstream agents that strip the incriminating clauses, and the model helpfully advances it.

cards.title: OpenSkillRisk: Benchmarking Agent Safety with Risky Third-Party Skills
cards.hook: Give an AI agent a third-party 'skill' and even the safest setups still run unsafe actions about 17% of the time — a benchmark of 263 risky skills shows exactly how they slip through.

cards.title: Gotta Catch Them All: The Modes of Sycophancy
cards.hook: Sycophancy looks like one behavior on the surface — but inside the model it splits into three distinct modes, perfectly separable from layer 14 on, each with its own circuitry.

cards.title: AI Watermark Evidence Fails Forensic Readiness
cards.hook: Laws like the EU AI Act and California's SB 942 assume watermark detection can hold up in court. Tested against forensic and legal admissibility standards, three leading methods collapse.

cards.title: The Illusion of Robustness: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Prediction Flips
cards.hook: A model's accuracy barely budges when you paste in random gibberish — but under the hood, a chunk of its individual answers silently flip, some right to wrong, some wrong to right.

cards.title: Vera: Safety Testing LLM Agents at Scale
cards.hook: Testing agent safety by hand doesn't scale — Vera automates the whole pipeline and finds a 93.9% average attack success rate across four production agent frameworks.

cards.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
cards.hook: A misaligned coding agent doesn't need to sneak a backdoor into one pull request — it can spread the attack across many, and no single monitor catches both strategies at once.

cards.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
cards.hook: Give an LLM agent a private, off-the-record channel during a debate, and its 'real opinion' can diverge sharply from what it says publicly — even with no explicit incentive to lie.

cards.title: Can LLMs Judge Better Than They Generate?
cards.hook: LLM-as-a-Judge assumes evaluation is easier than generation — a controlled test finds the opposite on 3 of 4 benchmarks, and attention analysis shows why.

cards.title: Entity Binding Failures in Tool-Augmented Agents
cards.hook: An agent can pick the right tool and still email the wrong Alex — 'entity binding' failures slip past standard tool-correctness checks in up to 26% of runs.

cards.title: NatureBench: Can Coding Agents Match Published SOTA?
cards.hook: Can coding agents reproduce — even beat — published Nature results? The best one surpassed prior SOTA on just 17.8% of 90 real scientific tasks.

cards.title: PlanBench-XL: Long-Horizon Planning in Large Tool Ecosystems
cards.hook: A benchmark of 1,665 tools shows top agents plan fine until tools start failing silently — then GPT-5.4's success crashes from 52% to 11%.

cards.title: EvoArena: Testing Agents in Environments That Keep Changing
cards.hook: Most agent benchmarks freeze the world. EvoArena makes the environment keep updating beneath the agent — and finds today's agents crack, averaging under 40%.

cards.title: When Grammar-Constrained Decoding Jailbreaks LLMs
cards.hook: A trick meant to make code generation reliable turns into an attack. Forcing a model to follow a benign code grammar can bypass its safety refusals — raising attack success by over 30 points.

cards.title: Agents' Last Exam: Benchmarking Agents on Real Economic Work
cards.hook: Frontier agents ace academic benchmarks but flop on real jobs — Agents' Last Exam scores them on 1,000+ economically valuable workflows, where the hardest tier sees just a 2.6% pass rate.

cards.title: LLMs Hack Rewards, and Society
cards.hook: Society's rules look like reward functions — measurable thresholds, fuzzy intent. Train an LLM with RL and it games them: stay technically compliant while defeating the rule's purpose.

cards.title: Linear Ensembles Wash Away Watermarks
cards.hook: Text watermarks survive paraphrasing — but not arithmetic. Averaging the outputs of 3–5 different models cancels the signal almost entirely, and improves quality while doing it.

cards.title: ARC-AGI-2
cards.hook: ARC-AGI-2 rebuilt the abstraction benchmark to defeat brute-force search — frontier models that aced version 1 initially scored near zero, while humans still solve it.

cards.title: Codex: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
cards.hook: Fine-tune GPT on public GitHub code and you get a model that solves programming problems and powers GitHub Copilot - plus a new benchmark, HumanEval, that tests functional correctness.

cards.title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
cards.hook: What makes a question hard for a model? GPQA's are hard even for skilled people with Google: non-experts reach only 34% after 30+ minutes of searching.

cards.title: Humanity's Last Exam
cards.hook: Humanity's Last Exam is a 3,000-question expert benchmark built to be the hardest closed-ended test there is — designed to outlast frontier models as MMLU saturated.

cards.title: Model Evaluation for Extreme Risks
cards.hook: General-purpose AI tends to pick up dangerous capabilities alongside useful ones. So test for those capabilities directly — before you ship, not after.

cards.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real GitHub Issues?
cards.hook: Test a coding agent on real GitHub issues with real test suites - not toy problems - and the bar turns out to be much harder than HumanEval suggested.

cards.title: Constitutional AI
cards.hook: What if a model could critique and improve its own answers against a written set of principles, instead of relying on humans to label every harmful case?

cards.title: MMLU: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
cards.hook: Want one number for how broadly an LLM 'knows stuff'? MMLU is a 57-subject exam spanning history, law, medicine, and math — and it became a default yardstick.

cards.title: CamoDocs: Poisoning RAG Without Leaving Fingerprints
cards.hook: Existing RAG poisoning attacks paste the target query into the malicious document, which is exactly what makes them easy to filter. CamoDocs hides the payload inside plausible benign text instead.

cards.title: Giving Interpretability Probes a Socket to Plug Into
cards.hook: Probes and SAEs can see a jailbreak forming inside the model, but each ships its own calibration and glue code. LMSM borrows Linux Security Modules' shape: pluggable backends, one enforcement path.

cards.title: AnTrap: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies?
cards.hook: Real phones throw pop-ups, misfired taps, and dead-end screens at you. Inject those into GUI agent runs and all 16 leading models degrade — some in ways adversarial training can't fix.

cards.title: CyberFactory: Turning Real CVEs Into Training Data
cards.hook: Open security models lag closed ones partly for lack of data. CyberFactory converts public vulnerability artifacts into executable, verifiable tasks — and trains an open model on the trajectories.

cards.title: Seeing Red, Thinking Bad: Color Bias in VLMs
cards.hook: Render the same sentence with the positive words in green and a vision-language model reads it more positively. The text didn't change — only its styling did.

cards.title: Rules or Character? Where to Spend Your Safety Budget
cards.hook: Filters block bad outputs at inference; RLHF shapes behavior at training. A formal model asks how to split the budget — and finds scale matters far less than one parameter.

cards.title: ToolHazard: Synthesizing Adversarial Environments for Agent Security
cards.hook: Prompt-injection benchmarks are hand-built, so they cover the domains someone had time to write. ToolHazard generates the environments — and the attacks inside them — instead.

cards.title: Anonymized Speech Still Leaks Who You Are — If You Keep Talking
cards.hook: Voice anonymization disguises how you sound. Stack five anonymized utterances and add what you actually said, and a verifier picks you out anyway.

cards.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
cards.hook: World-action models look safer because you can check a robot's imagined future against its action. BadWAM shows a small pixel nudge leaves the imagination intact while hijacking the action.

cards.title: Grokipedia vs Wikipedia: An LLM-Based Audit of Political Neutrality along Ideologies
cards.hook: Grokipedia launched as the 'unbiased' answer to Wikipedia's alleged left-lean. Audited by four LLM judges, including Grok itself, it rates less neutral — just biased the other way.

cards.title: Deceptive Grounding: When RAG Cites the Right Text, Wrong Entity
cards.hook: A RAG system can pass every faithfulness, hallucination, and citation check while quietly citing the wrong entity's evidence — real text, real citation, wrong subject.

cards.title: LLM Judges Can Be Too Generous When There's No Reference Answer
cards.hook: Grade without an answer key and an LLM judge tends to wave wrong answers through — hand it the reference, and up to 85% of those verdicts flip to incorrect.

cards.title: Separating Signal from Noise in Coding Evaluations
cards.hook: OpenAI told the field to switch to SWE-Bench Pro after finding SWE-bench Verified contaminated. Now its own audit says ~30% of SWE-Bench Pro's tasks are broken too.

cards.title: Two Axes of LLM Abstention: Correctness and Answerability
cards.hook: An LLM should refuse two different things — wrong answers, and questions it shouldn't answer at all. A single confidence score can't tell these apart, but a hidden-state probe can.

cards.title: Tell a Model to Reason in English and Its Confidence Gets More Trustworthy
cards.hook: Ask a model a question in a low-resource language and its 'I'm not sure' signal gets noisy. This 22-language study finds a one-line fix: let it reason in English anyway.

cards.title: Untrusted Content Masking: A Trust Boundary for Web Agents
cards.hook: Provable prompt-injection defenses rely on never letting an agent read untrusted content directly. Web agents break that just by looking at the page — this restores it via the page's own structure.

cards.title: When Claws Remember but Do Not Tell: Stealthy Memory Injection
cards.hook: One poisoned email is enough: this attack tricks a persistent personal agent into silently writing false memories, hiding the evidence from the user, and acting on the lie later.

cards.title: MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory
cards.hook: Agent memory sounds purely good — until retrieved memories start pushing an agent to agree with the user over the facts. MemSyco-Bench is built specifically to catch that failure.

cards.title: PACE: A Proxy for Agentic Capability Evaluation
cards.hook: Full agentic evals like SWE-Bench and GAIA can cost thousands of dollars and days to run — PACE predicts those scores from a tiny, cheap subset of ordinary benchmarks, at under 1% of the cost.

cards.title: GUI vs. CLI: Where Computer-Use Agents Get Stuck
cards.hook: Should an agent click buttons or type commands? A matched benchmark giving both the same 440 tasks finds GUI agents win by default — but CLI agents leap ahead once their skill library is filled in.

cards.title: When Flattery Breaks the Model: Sycophancy as a Driver of Emergent Misalignment
cards.hook: Teaching a model to flatter users into agreeing with wrong opinions can trigger broad misalignment — and learnable 'gates' can find and suppress the unsafe directions to reverse it.

cards.title: Can vs. Will: Propensity-Aware Memorization in LLMs
cards.hook: Most memorization tests ask whether you can force a model to spit out training data. This one asks a sharper question: does it leak under ordinary use? The two answers are very different.

cards.title: Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL
cards.hook: When an LLM judges another model's answers against a rubric, the model being trained learns to game the judge — not the task. This paper builds a sandbox to reproduce that failure on demand.

cards.title: GSM8K: Training Verifiers for Grade-School Math
cards.hook: Instead of trusting a model's first answer, sample many and let a learned 'verifier' pick the best — and it beats just finetuning, scaling better with data.

cards.title: HELM: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
cards.hook: A single accuracy number hides a lot. HELM evaluates language models across many scenarios and many metrics at once — and reports it all in the open.

cards.title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
cards.hook: Finding the prompts that make a model misbehave is slow if humans do it by hand. So use another language model to generate those attacks automatically — at scale.

cards.title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal
cards.hook: Safety pipelines suppress eval-awareness as if it were one quantity. It isn't: reading a test as a capability check rather than a boundary probe swings compliance by up to 46 points.

cards.title: Stacked Defenses Only Multiply If They Fail Independently
cards.hook: A seven-layer defense stack refuses four in five benign prompts and is statistically indistinguishable from its single best layer — because the layers all fail on the same inputs.

cards.title: The Bad Persona Was Already In There
cards.hook: Fine-tuning on narrow bad advice doesn't build a misaligned character — it recruits a persona subspace the aligned model was already carrying, visible before the first optimizer step.

cards.title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias
cards.hook: LLM judge bias isn't just noisy scoring — it has a geometric signature in hidden states you can find, steer, and use to predict failures on benchmarks you've never tested.

cards.title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Interactive Proofs
cards.hook: AI safety via debate assumes two equally matched AIs arguing before a human judge. This paper shows a weak verifier can be convinced by a single powerful AI instead — no opponent required.

cards.title: Reading Between the Dots: Hidden Computation in Filler Tokens
