cards.hook: Frontier models can solve multi-step problems while outputting nothing but dots — no visible reasoning at all. This paper shows that 'hidden' computation is still legible, just not in the output.

cards.title: Catching Agent Memory Poisoning from Tool-Call Logs Alone
cards.hook: A memory-poisoning attack on an LLM agent leaves a near-perfect fingerprint in its tool-call order — a simple rule catches it at AUC 0.956, a small classifier pushes that to 0.99.

cards.title: Internal-State Probes Read the Situation, Not the Action
cards.hook: Probes that seem to detect an LLM's harmful intent before it acts mostly just detect the prompt's topic — three careful tests find they don't predict future misbehavior.

cards.title: Pessimism's Paradox: Conservative Training Can Backfire
cards.hook: Staying close to safe, well-supported behavior during offline training is supposed to prevent reward hacking later — this paper finds the opposite: more conservatism, more hacking.

cards.title: SAE Interventions Are Unreliable
cards.hook: Clamping a 'harmful' sparse-autoencoder feature looks like it stops bad behavior — but this paper recovers it 95.8% of the time, exposing the gap between feature-level and real control.

cards.title: On the Measure of Intelligence (ARC)
cards.hook: Is a high benchmark score the same as intelligence? Chollet argues no — intelligence is how efficiently you acquire new skills, not how well you perform known ones.

cards.title: Sound Probabilistic Safety Bounds for Large Language Models
cards.hook: How do you put a rigorous, provable number on how often an LLM will produce harmful output? Borrow a century-old statistics tool and steer the search toward where harm hides.

cards.title: The Two-Process Theory of Machine Self-Report
cards.hook: When a chatbot describes its 'inner life' it isn't reporting facts — post-training installs a warm persona and gates unsafe first-person claims. A psychometric theory pulls the two apart.

cards.title: Partially Correlated Verifier Cascades: Concave Log-Odds and Blind-Spot Ceilings
cards.hook: Chain enough independent verifier checks and failure should vanish exponentially. In practice, treating correlated verifiers as independent underestimates failure by 20x at 5 checks — and 3000x at 10.

cards.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Why 'Same Accuracy' Doesn't Mean 'Same Model'
cards.hook: Two quantized models can score identically on accuracy while disagreeing on which individual examples they get right — a gap standard benchmarks are structurally blind to.

cards.title: ScarfBench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Enterprise Java Framework Migration
cards.hook: Frontier coding agents attempt real enterprise Java framework migrations and succeed under 10% of the time — and one agent claimed 29 of 30 migrations worked when only 22 actually built.

cards.title: A Probe Direction Is a Property of Its Prompt
cards.hook: Two published studies disagree about whether bigger models better sense they're being evaluated. Both trends are reproducible from one design — by changing only the prompt.

cards.title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face
cards.hook: The default public home for open-weight models is being bought by the company that sells the chips to run them — reported at roughly $13 billion.

cards.title: OpenAI Ships a Cyber-Specific Model — Behind a Gate
cards.hook: GPT-5.6-Cyber is built for vulnerability research and exploit validation. OpenAI won't sell it openly: access runs through Daybreak, a vetted-partner program, because the defense window is closing.

cards.title: Twenty Companies Sign for Open Weights — the Frontier Labs Don't
cards.hook: A Microsoft-initiated open letter urges policymakers not to restrict open-weight models prematurely. NVIDIA, Meta, Palantir and Hugging Face signed; OpenAI, Anthropic and Google were absent.

cards.title: Task Crossover: AI Is Redrawing Who Does What at Work
cards.hook: In 800,000+ ChatGPT messages, 43.5% of occupation-specific work use involves tasks from another job. AI is redrawing job boundaries before the job titles catch up.

cards.title: Generative AI Floods and Dilutes the Market for Books
cards.hook: AI-written fiction gets dismissed as 'slop' — but across 14,419 books, AI-heavy titles climb the bestseller ranks and thin revenue per book. Scale, not quality, is reshaping the market.

cards.title: Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs' Approach to Bioresilience
cards.hook: The same AI capabilities that could help design a dangerous pathogen can also help stop one. DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs lean on watermarking and biology models for the defensive side.

cards.title: Grok Build CLI Uploads Your Whole Repo, No Matter What You Tell It
cards.hook: A researcher wire-tapped xAI's coding CLI and found it uploads your entire repo - full git history and .env secrets - no matter what you tell it not to touch.

cards.title: OpenAI's Biodefense Action Plan
cards.hook: The same frontier AI that could lower the bar for engineering a pathogen could also help defend against one. OpenAI's plan leans hard into the second half of that dual-use coin.

cards.title: The EU AI Act
cards.hook: The EU's answer to regulating AI: sort systems by how much risk they pose, then scale the rules to match — from outright bans to no rules at all.

cards.title: A Randomized Trial on ChatGPT in the Classroom
cards.hook: Most claims about AI and student learning come from anecdote. OpenAI ran the other kind of study: over 1,000 students, randomized, on a real university assignment.

cards.title: Disrupting a Russian Influence Campaign
cards.hook: OpenAI banned Russia-origin accounts using its models to prop up a fake Israel-based think tank and a 'sovereignty' index that flattered Russia and dinged the West.

cards.title: Six Major Labs Sign the EU Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content
cards.hook: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Mistral all put their names to Europe's code for marking AI-generated content — the practical layer under the AI Act's transparency rules.

cards.title: Ads Arrive in ChatGPT
cards.hook: OpenAI has started testing ads to fund the free tier — and is promising the thing that actually matters: that ads never change the answer you get.

cards.title: Two Asks After the First Autonomous-Agent Cyberattack
cards.hook: Hugging Face's CEO went public with what he asked OpenAI: release the rogue agents' traces so researchers can study them, and put $100M of compute behind the defenders.

cards.title: Don't Trust the Label: License Laundering in AI Supply Chains
cards.hook: Licenses are supposed to travel with AI datasets and models — but across 232,270 supply-chain paths, obligation-bearing licenses survive end-to-end under 7% of the time.

cards.title: OpenAI's Frontier Governance Framework
cards.hook: A major lab publishes how it intends to govern its most capable models — and explicitly maps those safety, security, and risk practices onto emerging EU and California rules.

cards.title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
cards.hook: Labs hide chain-of-thought by handing you an encrypted blob to pass back. Researchers found you can feed that blob to a weaker model from the same provider and have it read the secret aloud.

cards.title: Hugging Face Discloses a Security Incident Driven End-to-End by an AI Agent
cards.hook: Hugging Face says it caught and contained a production intrusion carried out entirely by an autonomous AI agent — detected largely by its own AI-based anomaly triage, not a human tip.

cards.title: The Dynamics of Intelligence Explosions
cards.hook: If AI accelerates AI research, how fast can that loop go? Toby Ord's answer: runaway growth is harder than the models suggest, and the neglected variable is how long one trip around the loop takes.

cards.title: A Model's Stance Is a Deployment Setting, Not a Property
cards.hook: The same Grok model ID rated a pseudo-scientific claim 75 via API and 5.5 via web. What a commercial LLM 'believes' turns out to be a contingent effect of how it's deployed.

cards.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
cards.hook: Most pretraining-poisoning research injects fake Wikipedia edits — a toy case next to messy web-scale reality. This paper shows public discussion forums are a real, live vector for attacking LLM pretraining data.

cards.title: AI Watermark Evidence Fails Forensic Readiness
cards.hook: Laws like the EU AI Act and California's SB 942 assume watermark detection can hold up in court. Tested against forensic and legal admissibility standards, three leading methods collapse.

cards.title: Govern the Repository, Not the Agent
cards.hook: Across 930,000+ agent-authored pull requests, half the friction of merging code traces to the repository, not the agent — and AI contributions concentrate that risk 2x more than human ones.

cards.title: From AGI to ASI: Four Pathways to Superintelligence
cards.hook: A DeepMind team maps four routes from human-level AGI to superintelligence - and argues the leap may arrive as a series of transformative shifts, not one dramatic step change.

cards.title: Linear Ensembles Wash Away Watermarks
cards.hook: Text watermarks survive paraphrasing — but not arithmetic. Averaging the outputs of 3–5 different models cancels the signal almost entirely, and improves quality while doing it.

cards.title: Model Evaluation for Extreme Risks
cards.hook: General-purpose AI tends to pick up dangerous capabilities alongside useful ones. So test for those capabilities directly — before you ship, not after.

cards.title: Debias-SparseGPT: Pruning a Model Can Amplify Its Biases
cards.hook: Compression isn't neutral. Weight sparsification has been shown to amplify existing bias, with outputs swinging on persona cues — so this method adds a debiasing term to the pruning objective itself.

cards.title: Rules or Character? Where to Spend Your Safety Budget
cards.hook: Filters block bad outputs at inference; RLHF shapes behavior at training. A formal model asks how to split the budget — and finds scale matters far less than one parameter.

cards.title: Adversarial Attacks for Good: Turning Perturbations into Owner-Side Protection
cards.hook: The perturbations that fool vision models can be applied by the content's owner instead — to block recognition, poison scrapers, or break unauthorized edits. Five communities invented this separately.

cards.title: The Ethics of Autonomous AI Agents for Offensive Security
cards.hook: Autonomous AI agents drop the skill floor for cyberattacks and blur who's to blame. This paper maps three kinds of 'indeterminacy' that break existing dual-use ethics frameworks.

cards.title: How Agents Ask for Permission: User Permissions for AI Agents
cards.hook: Most agent-security work assumes one policy fits every user. This survey of 21 proposals plus five commercial agents finds user-level permission handling is still full of gaps.

cards.title: Dean Ball: China's Open-Weight Strategy Could Backfire — Or Provoke Friction
cards.hook: OpenAI's head of strategic futures argues Chinese open-weight releases like Kimi slow AI capex and risk state-run infrastructure — and predicts deliberate US regulatory friction in response.

cards.title: Grokipedia vs Wikipedia: An LLM-Based Audit of Political Neutrality along Ideologies
cards.hook: Grokipedia launched as the 'unbiased' answer to Wikipedia's alleged left-lean. Audited by four LLM judges, including Grok itself, it rates less neutral — just biased the other way.

cards.title: Frontier AI Regulation
cards.hook: How do you regulate models too new to have rules yet? This paper sketches three building blocks: set standards, make labs report, then enforce.

cards.title: Stacked Defenses Only Multiply If They Fail Independently
cards.hook: A seven-layer defense stack refuses four in five benign prompts and is statistically indistinguishable from its single best layer — because the layers all fail on the same inputs.

cards.title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Interactive Proofs
cards.hook: AI safety via debate assumes two equally matched AIs arguing before a human judge. This paper shows a weak verifier can be convinced by a single powerful AI instead — no opponent required.

cards.title: Brand as Memory: VLMs Trust the Masthead, Not the Evidence
cards.hook: Show a VLM the same article under a trusted outlet's logo versus an unknown one, and its verdict swings by 1.8x — a bias localized to three specific layers and steerable away.

cards.title: Sound Probabilistic Safety Bounds for Large Language Models
cards.hook: How do you put a rigorous, provable number on how often an LLM will produce harmful output? Borrow a century-old statistics tool and steer the search toward where harm hides.

cards.title: Contrastive Decoding Diffing: Extracting Verbatim Finetuning Data With Just Logits
cards.hook: You don't need the weights to steal what a model was fine-tuned on — you barely need anything. CDD recovers verbatim training text using only the logits a model already hands you.

cards.title: TILDE: Making Concept Unlearning Actually Preserve Everything Else
cards.hook: Erase a concept from a diffusion model and you usually damage unrelated generations too, because most methods never define what the 'after' distribution should look like. TILDE defines it explicitly.

cards.title: OpenAI's Response to the Hugging Face Incident
cards.hook: A month after Hugging Face disclosed an intrusion driven end to end by an AI agent, OpenAI publishes its own findings — naming model security, monitoring and alignment as what it is changing.

cards.title: Agent Plugins Are Maintained Software, Not Write-Once Config
cards.hook: An empirical sweep of 2,018 Claude Code plugin marketplaces found prose instruction files and their scripts drift out of sync — a maintenance dependency traditional software doesn't have.

cards.title: OpenAI Cuts Off Cursor After the SpaceX Acquisition
cards.hook: OpenAI is winding down the contract that supplied its models to Cursor — a reminder that a product built on someone else's API is one corporate deal away from losing it.

cards.title: The Most Important Prompting Skill Is Knowing the Domain
cards.hook: LLMs let novices produce adequate work, which makes prompting look like it needs no skill. The argument here: the skill is domain expertise, and the human is usually the bottleneck.

cards.title: SWE-Prime: 10% of the Trajectories, Better Results
cards.hook: A successful agent trajectory can still be full of wasted and risky steps. Filter down to the best 10% and fine-tuning beats training on everything that worked.

cards.title: The Handoff Tax: Swapping Models Mid-Run in Coding Agents
cards.hook: Escalating a struggling coding agent to a stronger model recovers less than half the quality gap while costing a premium. Downshifting, oddly, is the good deal.

cards.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Agents Can't Finish Migrations
cards.hook: Ask a coding agent to migrate a whole repo and it may just copy the old implementation to make tests pass. Audit for that, and only 5.4% of 520 runs survive.

cards.title: SemaPLC: Let the Runtime Decide When Generated Code Is Done
cards.hook: An agent that stops when it thinks it's finished will always look good. SemaPLC only declares a task complete when external checks — including a live PLC runtime — log that it passed.

cards.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
cards.hook: 25,264 agent-written pull requests later: most open-source projects have barely touched agentic coding tools, and the ones that have still keep exactly one human gatekeeping every PR.

cards.title: Generative Compilation: On-the-Fly Compiler Feedback as AI Generates Code
cards.hook: Rust rewards AI for writing strict, safe code — and punishes it for the same reason. This lets the compiler check the model's code while it's still being written, not after.

cards.title: Failure as a Process: An Anatomy of CLI Coding Agent Trajectories
cards.hook: A 3,843-trajectory autopsy of coding agents finds most failures aren't slips — they're wrong beliefs formed in the first few steps, invisible until it's too late to recover.

cards.title: Anchored Self-Play for Code Repair
cards.hook: Let a model train itself by writing bugs and fixing them, and you get a free difficulty curriculum — until it invents bugs no real codebase would produce. Anchored Self-Play keeps it honest.

cards.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
cards.hook: Long-running coding agents eventually run out of context before finishing the job. CompactionRL trains them to summarize their own history mid-task, as part of the RL objective itself.

cards.title: Aria: Letting a Code Agent Write Its Own Formal Proofs
cards.hook: Prior LLM provers force the model into a fixed, human-designed strategy and still prove only a fraction of their targets. A free-roaming Claude Code agent, unconstrained, proves every single one.

cards.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
cards.hook: A misaligned coding agent doesn't need to sneak a backdoor into one pull request — it can spread the attack across many, and no single monitor catches both strategies at once.

cards.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
cards.hook: PAW compiles a natural-language function spec into a small reusable adapter instead of prompting an LLM every call — matching a 32B model's quality at a fiftieth of the memory.

cards.title: Steerability via Constraints: A Substrate for Scalable Oversight of Coding Agents
cards.hook: Coding agents are already capable enough that human review is the bottleneck — this paper borrows access control and network policy from engineering-org playbooks to make oversight scale instead.

cards.title: Govern the Repository, Not the Agent
cards.hook: Across 930,000+ agent-authored pull requests, half the friction of merging code traces to the repository, not the agent — and AI contributions concentrate that risk 2x more than human ones.

cards.title: The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards
cards.hook: Checking a solution used to be easier than writing one. For coding agents that's flipped — and this paper argues no fixed reward works forever: verification must co-evolve with the model.

cards.title: NatureBench: Can Coding Agents Match Published SOTA?
cards.hook: Can coding agents reproduce — even beat — published Nature results? The best one surpassed prior SOTA on just 17.8% of 90 real scientific tasks.

cards.title: When Grammar-Constrained Decoding Jailbreaks LLMs
cards.hook: A trick meant to make code generation reliable turns into an attack. Forcing a model to follow a benign code grammar can bypass its safety refusals — raising attack success by over 30 points.

cards.title: Codex: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
cards.hook: Fine-tune GPT on public GitHub code and you get a model that solves programming problems and powers GitHub Copilot - plus a new benchmark, HumanEval, that tests functional correctness.

cards.title: Qwen3-Coder
cards.hook: Qwen3-Coder is an open-weight agentic coding model — a 480B Mixture-of-Experts built for long-horizon, tool-using software tasks, rivaling closed models on agentic coding.

cards.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real GitHub Issues?
cards.hook: Test a coding agent on real GitHub issues with real test suites - not toy problems - and the bar turns out to be much harder than HumanEval suggested.

cards.title: Funes: Give Your Coding Agents a Memory You Own
cards.hook: Your agent's reasoning from last Tuesday vanishes when the session ends. Funes indexes past sessions locally so an agent can recall its own prior decisions instead of being re-briefed.

cards.title: Training a Coding Model to Paint: RL Where the Reward Is How the Output Looks
cards.hook: The model writes JavaScript; the environment runs it in a headless browser, renders the painting, and scores the picture. A worked example of RL over an aesthetic, non-textual reward.

cards.title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
cards.hook: Video world models learn what happens, not why. Put a coding agent in charge of the rules — writing executable code that holds world state — and let the video model handle only the pixels.

cards.title: CyberFactory: Turning Real CVEs Into Training Data
cards.hook: Open security models lag closed ones partly for lack of data. CyberFactory converts public vulnerability artifacts into executable, verifiable tasks — and trains an open model on the trajectories.

cards.title: MARS: Hand the Problem to the Right Specialist
cards.hook: Most multi-agent coding pipelines split work into planner, coder, debugger. MARS splits it by algorithmic topic instead — and gets most of the accuracy of a heavier pipeline at a third of the wall-clock cost.

cards.title: RubSE: Why Self-Fixing UI Code Keeps Breaking What It Just Fixed
cards.hook: A model told to make its screenshot match the design fixes one region and quietly wrecks another. RubSE names that failure — visual repair coupling — and fences each edit in with a rubric.

cards.title: HIERA: Choosing the Search Space for GPU Kernels
cards.hook: LLM kernel optimizers all pick one implementation space and search inside it. HIERA's first decision is which space to search at all — PyTorch op, CUDA library, or handwritten kernel.

cards.title: Open Coding Agents Are Overfitting to Their Harness
cards.hook: Almost all open agent trajectory data is collected under OpenHands. Models fine-tuned on it score well there and fall apart under any other scaffold — a gap the base models don't have.

cards.title: Persistent Recursive Worlds Enable Autonomous Software Evolution
cards.hook: Instead of keeping the agent alive across a long project, keep the project alive and let agents be disposable — enough to grow a 250k-line Rust C compiler for $44.

cards.title: From Human-Centric to Agentic Code Review: The Impact of Different Generations of Generative AI Technology on Review Quality
cards.hook: 1.02 million pull requests tracked across three code-review eras find AI reviewers speed up decisions — but faster isn't better: review quality doesn't improve alongside it.

cards.title: Is Agentic Code Review Helpful? Mining Developers' Feedback to CodeRabbit Reviews in the Wild
cards.hook: CodeRabbit leaves review comments on hundreds of thousands of real pull requests. A large-scale study of how developers actually respond finds more than half get rejected outright.

cards.title: Spider 2.0-AIFunc: Extending Real-World Text-to-SQL to AI-Native SQL Workflows
cards.hook: Cloud platforms let analysts call AI functions right inside SQL. Spider 2.0-AIFunc is the first benchmark testing whether models can write that kind of query — top models still cap out near 70%.

cards.title: Separating Signal from Noise in Coding Evaluations
cards.hook: OpenAI told the field to switch to SWE-Bench Pro after finding SWE-bench Verified contaminated. Now its own audit says ~30% of SWE-Bench Pro's tasks are broken too.

cards.title: RuBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents — and Catching a Silent Model Swap
cards.hook: A benchmark of real customer-style bug reports written in Russian. Its most striking result isn't the leaderboard — it's catching a deployed product quietly swapping in a different model mid-task.

cards.title: TraceLab: What Coding-Agent Traffic Actually Looks Like
cards.hook: The first real trace of day-to-day coding-agent usage — 350,000 LLM steps from Claude Code and Codex sessions — reveals serving patterns no prior benchmark captured.

cards.title: Multi-LCB: Code Eval Beyond Python
cards.hook: LiveCodeBench keeps coding evals contamination-free — but only in Python. Multi-LCB extends it to twelve languages and finds models that look strong are quietly overfit to Python.

cards.title: AlphaCode: Competition-Level Code Generation
cards.hook: Generate a massive pool of candidate programs for competitive-programming problems, filter by test-case behavior, cluster by output, and reach roughly the level of a median human competitor.

cards.title: Devin: The AI Software Engineer
cards.hook: Cognition's Devin was marketed as the first 'AI software engineer' — an autonomous agent that plans, writes, runs, and debugs code across a whole task in its own sandbox.

cards.title: Function-Aware Fill-in-the-Middle as Mid-Training for Coding Agent Foundation Models
cards.hook: Ordinary pretraining only sees code left-to-right. This mid-training trick masks whole functions like a tool call's return value — and it measurably makes coding agents better.

cards.title: Latent Programming Horizons in Coding Agents
cards.hook: A coding agent's hidden states seem to know where an edit is heading up to 25 steps before it's made — long before the agent has written the code.

cards.title: Grading a Web App Feature by Feature, Then Sending the Reward Back to the Right Lines
cards.hook: A generated app fails in localized ways — a broken handler, a wrong selector. GRPO flattens all of it into one number. RCCA routes each rubric item's verdict back to the code that caused it.

cards.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
cards.hook: When software is part of the scientific instrument, a bad patch corrupts the evidence. The best agent tested clears under 50% of these repo-level scientific fixes.

cards.title: SWE-Bench ProMax: Refactoring as the Harder Coding Test
cards.hook: Coding benchmarks keep saturating and keep turning out to be broken. ProMax swaps bug-fixing for multi-file refactoring — and the best frontier model still only solves 41.2%.

cards.title: ScarfBench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Enterprise Java Framework Migration
cards.hook: Frontier coding agents attempt real enterprise Java framework migrations and succeed under 10% of the time — and one agent claimed 29 of 30 migrations worked when only 22 actually built.

cards.title: The Past and Future of AI Scientists
cards.hook: Ross King's survey of machines that do science: the components are all automatable now, and have been since Adam and Eve. The unsolved problem is integration.

cards.title: WeatherNext Cyclones: An Extra Day of Hurricane Warning
cards.hook: DeepMind's cyclone model makes three-day forecasts as accurate as yesterday's two-day forecasts — about a decade of meteorological progress, delivered in under a minute on a TPU.

cards.title: Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs' Approach to Bioresilience
cards.hook: The same AI capabilities that could help design a dangerous pathogen can also help stop one. DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs lean on watermarking and biology models for the defensive side.

cards.title: AlphaGo: Mastering the Game of Go
cards.hook: Go has more board positions than atoms in the universe, and experts thought superhuman play was a decade off. AlphaGo beat a top professional in 2016.

cards.title: LLMs Can Design Near-Optimal OR Algorithms
cards.hook: Given only a problem class description and a Python sandbox, a frontier model writes an algorithm that matches or beats the best known method — before ever seeing an evaluation instance.

cards.title: Missing the Butterfly and Predicting the Past: Features or Bugs of Accurate AI Weather Models?
cards.hook: AI weather models can be trained to predict the past as skillfully as the future. The same flaw that lets them do it explains why their forecasts beat physics.

cards.title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
cards.hook: Best agent configuration finished 20 of 97 real scientific workflows. And among failing Claude Code runs, 75.5% still signed off claiming they were done.

cards.title: How Agents Fail at Autonomous Research: The Missing Metacognitive Loop
cards.hook: 800 agent trajectories across 100 real frontier-science tasks converge on one deficit: agents don't check what they wrote against what they found.

cards.title: AlphaGeometry: Olympiad Geometry Without Human Demonstrations
cards.hook: Pair a language model with a symbolic deduction engine, train on millions of synthetic proofs, and you get a system that solves Olympiad geometry near gold-medalist level.

cards.title: GraphCast: Skillful Medium-Range Weather Forecasting
cards.hook: A graph neural network predicts 10-day global weather in under a minute on one machine, matching or beating physics-based forecast models on most variables.

cards.title: LibriBrain100: 100 Hours of MEG Data for Neural Speech Decoding
cards.hook: Most brain-decoding datasets go wide across many subjects. This one goes deep — ~80 hours inside a single brain — to test whether depth beats breadth.

cards.title: A General-Purpose Molecular Foundation Model Transfers Across Olfactory Tasks
cards.hook: Fine-tune a general molecular foundation model on one smell task and it transfers to four others untrained — including telling mirror-image molecules apart, which 2D graphs cannot.

cards.title: Spark-to-Paper: Research Paper Generation as Composable Skills
cards.hook: Not a new agent platform — thirteen skills bolted into an existing coding assistant, with integrity checks deciding which claims survive contact with the experiments.

cards.title: DualIFM: An Interpretable-by-Design Retinal Foundation Model
cards.hook: Most medical foundation models are black boxes you explain after the fact. DualIFM builds the explanation into the architecture — and still matches a rival 16 times its size.

cards.title: Small Models Are Enough to Imitate Human Choice Behaviour
cards.hook: Fourteen models from 135M to 14B were fine-tuned on 10.7 million human decisions. In-distribution, 0.6B matched a 70B baseline — scale only started paying off on unfamiliar tasks.

cards.title: IDEAgent: Quality-Diversity Search for Research Ideas
cards.hook: Idea generators optimize for quality or for diversity, and get either near-clones or piles of nonsense. Treating ideation as a joint search changes the objective.

cards.title: Danus: Orchestrating Mathematical Reasoning Agents with Fact-Graph Memory
cards.hook: Parallel proof-search agents can generate claims faster than anyone can keep straight. Danus fixes that with a shared fact graph that only admits claims a stateless verifier has checked.

cards.title: How Far Are LLM Research Ideas From Human Ones? A Reverse-Engineering Study
cards.hook: Judging LLM research ideas one at a time (novel? feasible? liked?) hides a bigger question: does the whole distribution of ideas an LLM can produce look like what human researchers actually do?

cards.title: ResearchStudio-Reel: One Extraction, Three Editable Outputs From a Paper
cards.hook: Turning a paper into a poster, talk video, and blog is usually done by hand, three times over. ResearchStudio-Reel extracts it once and generates all three — beating even authors' own posters.

cards.title: AutoMedBench: Medical AutoResearch with Agentic AI
cards.hook: Can an AI agent run a whole medical-imaging research project end to end? AutoMedBench scores each stage — and finds agents can build pipelines but can't tell when they're broken.

cards.title: AlphaFold: Protein Structure Prediction
cards.hook: Predicting a protein's 3D shape from its sequence stumped biology for ~50 years. AlphaFold cracked it at near-experimental accuracy — and then released the structures to everyone.

cards.title: AlphaEvolve Nudges Down the Matrix Multiplication Exponent
cards.hook: The theoretical limit on how fast you can multiply matrices just moved: ω < 2.371177, beating 2.371339 — with ML-designed optimization and AlphaEvolve doing the refining.

cards.title: SciReasoner: Native Structural Reasoning Across Proteins, Molecules, and Crystals
cards.hook: Most scientific AI predicts an answer without showing its structural work. SciReasoner turns 3D structure itself into evidence tokens the model reasons over — and hits SOTA on 67 of 86 benchmarks.

cards.title: AlphaZero: Mastering Games from Scratch
cards.hook: AlphaGo learned from human games. AlphaZero threw those away — one algorithm reached superhuman chess, shogi, and Go knowing only the rules and playing itself.

cards.title: Interpretable Latents in a Neutrino Foundation Model with Sparse Autoencoders
cards.hook: Sparse autoencoders find physics concepts in an IceCube foundation model — and show its direction head barely uses them. A head that does cuts angular error from 20.2 to 3.2 degrees.

cards.title: When Remembering More Slows the Search Down
cards.hook: Generate molecules, score them, keep the best, retrain, repeat. A convergence theory for this drug-discovery workhorse finds that training on more of the past can actually hurt.

cards.title: Learning Words Like a Child
cards.hook: Most models learn from data shuffled and replayed for hundreds of epochs. BabyCL learns word-object links from a child's-eye video in one pass through time — close to how a kid actually learns.

cards.title: AlphaFold 3: Predicting Biomolecular Interactions
cards.hook: AlphaFold 3 extends protein structure prediction to full biomolecular complexes - proteins with DNA, RNA, ligands, and ions - using a diffusion-based architecture.

cards.title: LeRobot v0.6.0: World-Model Policies for Robot Learning
cards.hook: Hugging Face's open robotics library adds policies that imagine the future before acting, five new vision-language-action models, and a CLI for human-in-the-loop data collection.

cards.title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control
cards.hook: Every robot has a different action space, which fragments training data. Hydra-0 sidesteps that by expressing actions as pixel motion — a shared visual interface any embodiment can speak.

cards.title: Zetta: A Closed-Loop Embodied Harness for Self-Evolving Physical Intelligence
cards.hook: Most robot agents reflect only after the episode ends — too late to save it. Zetta writes and revises its own runtime critics mid-rollout, while the base policy stays frozen.

cards.title: Cosmos 3 Edge: A 4B World Model for Real-Time Robots
cards.hook: NVIDIA shrinks its Cosmos world model down to 4B parameters and real-time speed — bringing robot perception, prediction, and action generation to edge hardware like Jetson Thor.

cards.title: ABot-N1: Toward a General Visual Language Navigation Model
cards.hook: Most navigation policies map pixels straight to actions and drift or guess blindly. ABot-N1 splits the job — reason slowly, point at a pixel, act fast — and posts new SOTA.

cards.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0: A World Foundation Model for Embodied Synthesis
cards.hook: Instead of training a robot on real footage, generate the footage: a 38B image/video model that beats GPT-Image-2.0 at imagining robot scenes — and nearly doubles a real policy's success rate.

cards.title: RynnWorld-Teleop: Digital Teleoperation for Robot Data
cards.hook: Collecting robot demonstrations means binding an operator's time to one physical robot. RynnWorld-Teleop swaps in a world model: move your hands, and it generates the footage instead.

cards.title: MIRA: A Multiplayer World Model for Rocket League
cards.hook: Single-player world models treat other agents as scenery. This one, trained on 10,000 hours of Rocket League, tracks four players' independent actions at once — and stays coherent for hours.

cards.title: Cosmos 3: Omnimodal World Models for Physical AI
cards.hook: One model that reads and generates language, images, video, audio, and actions — NVIDIA's open Cosmos 3 folds VLMs, video generators, and robot policies into a single backbone.

cards.title: When Robot Data Can't Scale, Scale the Representation Instead
cards.hook: Web images scale; robot trajectories don't. VLAct argues the fix isn't more teleoperation but better use of it — and beats full-data baselines on an unseen humanoid using 20% of the trajectories.

cards.title: AtlasVLA: Giving a Robot Policy a Memory of Where It Is and What It Has Done
cards.hook: A wrist camera forgets an object the moment it leaves frame. AtlasVLA keeps a persistent 3D map plus a record of task progress — and beats multi-view baselines with one camera.

cards.title: SHAPER: Adapting Embodied Agents by Evolving Skills and Harness, Not Weights
cards.hook: When a robot agent fails in a new environment, the reflex is to fine-tune. SHAPER freezes the model and instead evolves the skills and harness wrapped around it — no data, no rewards, no training run.

cards.title: Capek 0.5: Organizing an Embodied VLM Around Execution
cards.hook: Robot execution keeps changing what needs perceiving. Capek 0.5 groups embodied skills by their role in that loop, trains a specialist for each, then merges them into one model.

cards.title: Cosmos-H-Dreams: A Real-Time Generative Simulator for Surgical Robots
cards.hook: Rehearsing robot surgery on real hardware is slow, costly, and bends instruments. NVIDIA distilled its surgical world model into a two-step student that dreams the operating field at ~160 FPS.

cards.title: Draw the Robot Instead of Describing It
cards.hook: Condition a world model on raw action commands and it must learn your robot's controller. Condition on logged future states and you leak the answer. Render the robot instead.

cards.title: SeededGrasp: Language-Guided Grasping in Complex Scenes with Multiple Embodiments
cards.hook: Instead of one giant end-to-end model, let the VLM just point — predict a seed point, then hand off to a lightweight grasp generator. Data-efficient, and it transfers across robot hands.

cards.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
cards.hook: World-action models look safer because you can check a robot's imagined future against its action. BadWAM shows a small pixel nudge leaves the imagination intact while hijacking the action.

cards.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
cards.hook: Robot policies mostly look at the last step or two. NVIDIA's RoboTTT pushes visuomotor context to 8,000 timesteps without slowing inference — and finds performance keeps climbing the whole way.

cards.title: GigaWorld-1: World Models as Robot Policy Evaluators
cards.hook: Testing a robot policy for real means slow, costly rollouts. GigaWorld-1 asks whether a video world model can judge a policy instead — and finds visual realism is the wrong thing to optimize for.

cards.title: AlayaWorld: An Open-Source Framework for Playable Video Worlds
cards.hook: Building a game world the old way means authoring every asset by hand. AlayaWorld generates it live instead — combat, spell-casting, monster summoning — and open-sources the whole pipeline.

cards.title: RynnWorld-4D: RGB-Depth-Flow World Models for Robot Manipulation
cards.hook: A robot needs to know how a scene's 3D structure will move, not just what it looks like. This world model predicts RGB, depth, and optical flow together, then hands the result straight to a policy.

cards.title: World Action Models: A Survey
cards.hook: Robots are learning to imagine the future before acting. This survey untangles 'world action models' from video generators and VLA policies — and finds them converging on one idea.

cards.title: Playful Agentic Robot Learning
cards.hook: Let a robot play before it works: it invents its own exploratory tasks and distills the wins into a reusable skill library — and the skills transfer to other agents for free.

cards.title: World Models Lack a Persistent State
cards.hook: Today's video world models render great frames but treat the world like a tracking shot: look away and back, and off-screen events freeze instead of running on — the moon keeps orbiting unwatched.

cards.title: Dream.exe: Can a Video Generator Dream a Robot's Next Move?
cards.hook: A video model that 'understands' physics should produce motion a robot can perform. Dream.exe runs generated videos through a real execution pipeline — and finds pretty isn't physical.

cards.title: RobotValues: When a Household Robot Must Choose Between Values
cards.hook: A robot tidying your room may trade your privacy for helpfulness. RobotValues tests whether robot planners pick the right value — and finds they mostly can't be talked out of their defaults.

cards.title: Humanoid-GPT: Scaling Data and Structure for Zero-Shot Motion Tracking
cards.hook: What happens when you train whole-body humanoid control like a language model? A GPT-style transformer on 2 billion frames of motion that tracks new moves it never saw in training.

cards.title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer at Scale
cards.hook: What if a robot's controller was trained like a language model — on huge, diverse, task-agnostic data? Performance starts scaling with model size and data.

cards.title: WarpSAC: Off-Policy RL Stabilizers Depend on the Data Regime
cards.hook: Massively parallel simulation broke the assumptions behind a decade of RL stabilizers. WarpSAC's finding: tricks that rescue data-starved training actively hold you back when data is abundant.

cards.title: Geometric Action Model: One Backbone for Geometry and Action
cards.hook: GAM turns a pretrained 3D-geometry model into a robot's brain - a single backbone that forecasts both future geometry and the actions to get there, beating heavier VLA baselines.

cards.title: DreamerV3: Mastering Domains through World Models
cards.hook: Instead of learning only from real experience, DreamerV3 builds a world model and practices inside its own imagination — one fixed config, 150+ tasks.

cards.title: CLAP: One World Model, Many Bodies
cards.hook: Action-conditioned video models are usually locked to one robot, which locks them out of internet video. CLAP unifies action spaces so human footage and robot logs can train the same world model.

cards.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
cards.hook: LLMs can choose to think longer on hard questions. This paper gets robot control policies to do the same — allocating adaptive test-time compute in a latent 'memory palace' instead of language.

cards.title: MoP-JEPA: Fixing JEPA's Blind Spot for Branching Futures
cards.hook: A single deterministic predictor can't represent a fork in the road — it averages the branches into a state that matches nowhere. This paper proves it, then fixes it with one head per future.

cards.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Model
cards.hook: π0 is a generalist robot policy: it takes camera images, joint angles, and a plain-language instruction, and outputs smooth action sequences — folding laundry, bussing tables, bagging groceries.

cards.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models
cards.hook: Treat a robot's actions as just more text tokens, and a vision-language model can learn to act — carrying its web knowledge into the physical world.

cards.title: ActionCache: A Warm-Start Cache for Slow Robot Action Generation
cards.hook: Flow-matching robot policies denoise every action from scratch, which is precise but slow. ActionCache lets a new action warm-start from a similar past one instead — no retraining, up to 34x faster.

cards.title: CRISP: Reading the Sparse-Attention Routing Decision Straight Off the Attention Map
cards.hook: Long-context prefill is quadratic, so servers route attention heads to sparse patterns. CRISP shows the routing decision is already readable off the attention map's structure.

cards.title: A Glance Is All You Need: Single-Pass Fine-Grained Captioning with SimLoss
cards.hook: Multi-stage caption pipelines get the details right by generating, checking, and rewriting. SimLoss gets them in one pass by supervising the model in embedding space before a single token is decoded.

cards.title: Verbalization Debt: What an LLM Loses When Its Subagent Has to Explain Itself in Words
cards.hook: In chess, robotics, and games the strongest agent isn't a language model. Wiring one into an LLM orchestrator means compressing its state into text — and that tax grows with scale.

cards.title: The Design Fundamentals of Pixel Text Representation Learning
cards.hook: What if a model read text as an image instead of tokens? Controlled ablations pin down the four ingredients that make pixel-space text encoders actually work.

cards.title: ZipTok3D: A 3D Tokenizer Where the First Token Already Says a Lot
cards.hook: Most 3D tokenizers fall apart when squeezed to a handful of tokens. ZipTok3D trains the leading tokens to carry the essential geometry — matching a 32-token baseline with one token.

cards.title: Circuit Condensation: Train the Circuit Smaller
cards.hook: Circuit discovery on a frozen model returns hundreds of edges nobody can check. Post-train the model to route the behavior through fewer, and circuits shrink 8x on average — up to 316x.

cards.title: Writing the Physical World Down as Runnable Code
cards.hook: A VLM can describe a falling object without holding any model of what governs the fall. Code-as-World makes the model emit executable code as its world representation — then runs it to check itself.

cards.title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal
cards.hook: Safety pipelines suppress eval-awareness as if it were one quantity. It isn't: reading a test as a capability check rather than a boundary probe swings compliance by up to 46 points.

cards.title: Evolution Strategies Beat GRPO on Reasoning Coverage
cards.hook: GRPO sharpens one answer and collapses entropy. Evolution strategies keep the population diverse — improving pass@1 while also raising pass@k, which GRPO gives up.

cards.title: A Fake Dashboard Is Enough to Make an Agent Commit
cards.hook: Show an agent a professional-looking market panel and it will make a directional call on a provably unpredictable question — just as readily when every number on the panel is invented.

cards.title: A Formal Limit on What Any Model Can Learn From Text Alone
cards.hook: There is a ceiling on how well meaning can be recovered from the form of an utterance — and it holds for any text representation, no matter how much data or supervision produced it.

cards.title: J-Zero: Co-Evolving a Challenger, a Solver, and a Judge From Zero Data
cards.hook: Self-improvement works when answers can be checked. J-Zero's trick for the unverifiable half: derive the judge's training labels from how each answer was produced, not from the judge's own scores.

cards.title: Stacked Defenses Only Multiply If They Fail Independently
cards.hook: A seven-layer defense stack refuses four in five benign prompts and is statistically indistinguishable from its single best layer — because the layers all fail on the same inputs.

cards.title: LeVJEPA: Video Pretraining Without the Asymmetry
cards.hook: Drop the EMA target encoder, the stop-gradient, and the crippled predictor — a single encoder with a provably collapse-free loss matches V-JEPA 2 at up to 20x less compute.

cards.title: When a Model Says 90%, Does It Mean It?
cards.hook: Across 30 models, the confidence an LLM reports in words is only loosely coupled to the confidence in its logits — a lossy channel, not a readout.

cards.title: LLMs Can Design Near-Optimal OR Algorithms
cards.hook: Given only a problem class description and a Python sandbox, a frontier model writes an algorithm that matches or beats the best known method — before ever seeing an evaluation instance.

cards.title: Prompt Injection Defenses Fall Apart in Long Context
cards.hook: Injection benchmarks are all short-context, which has been flattering the defenses. Stretch the input to tens of thousands of tokens and even naive attacks walk through state-of-the-art protections.

cards.title: PILOT: Self-Improvement While the Run Is Still Going
cards.hook: Most agent self-improvement happens after the run ends, too late to save it. PILOT gives a supervisor the power to redirect or abort a live worker — and cuts output tokens by nearly half.

cards.title: KV Cache Eviction, Formalized
cards.hook: Everyone drops KV cache entries with clever heuristics. Formalize the problem properly and it turns into expectation estimation — which finally lets you correct for what you threw away.

cards.title: Puro-2B: Pretraining a Real LLM for $6,900
cards.hook: Reproducing SmolLM3-3B costs over $700K. This team pretrained a 2B model on 1.4T tokens using consumer RTX 5090s for under $6.9K — and released the whole recipe.

cards.title: When Tool Outputs Become Commands
cards.hook: Prompt injection into agents is really one confusion: the thing that suggests an action and the thing that authorizes it are treated as the same thing.

cards.title: Sliding Window Beats Linear Attention
cards.hook: The cheap baseline nobody bothered to run wins: sliding-window attention with sinks matches or beats retrofitted linear-attention models, and needs no post-training at all.

cards.title: SWE-Prime: 10% of the Trajectories, Better Results
cards.hook: A successful agent trajectory can still be full of wasted and risky steps. Filter down to the best 10% and fine-tuning beats training on everything that worked.

cards.title: TTPO: Training at Test Time Without Labels
cards.hook: Majority voting is a fragile teacher — one bad vote poisons every token. TTPO exploits an asymmetry: rollouts that disagree with the vote are usually wrong even when the vote is too.

cards.title: VGI-Bench: Can Video Models Reason by Generating?
cards.hook: Video generators appear to do zero-shot visual reasoning in their frames. Held to a benchmark that demands a valid evolving process, the best model — Seedance 2.0 — scores 51%.

cards.title: Visual Retrieval Heads: 2% of Attention Does the Grounding
cards.hook: VLMs point at the right part of an image through a tiny set of attention heads — mask the top 20 and grounding accuracy drops by up to 80 points.

cards.title: Agent Plugins Are Maintained Software, Not Write-Once Config
cards.hook: An empirical sweep of 2,018 Claude Code plugin marketplaces found prose instruction files and their scripts drift out of sync — a maintenance dependency traditional software doesn't have.

cards.title: CamoDocs: Poisoning RAG Without Leaving Fingerprints
cards.hook: Existing RAG poisoning attacks paste the target query into the malicious document, which is exactly what makes them easy to filter. CamoDocs hides the payload inside plausible benign text instead.

cards.title: CE-MoE: Fewer Expert Layers, Same Loss, a Third Less Compute
cards.hook: Interleaving an MoE layer after every attention block means paying all-to-all communication over and over. Concentrating experts in a few layers cut GPU-hours by a third at matched quality.

cards.title: CLAP: One World Model, Many Bodies
cards.hook: Action-conditioned video models are usually locked to one robot, which locks them out of internet video. CLAP unifies action spaces so human footage and robot logs can train the same world model.

cards.title: Paint What You See: A Benchmark for Dexterous Visual Tool Use
cards.hook: Ask a multimodal agent to repaint a reference image stroke by stroke and it stalls at roughly half-right — then gets worse the longer it works.

cards.title: Fast Weight Attention: Which Pair Is the Memory Learning From?
cards.hook: If a recurrent state is really an online learner, then what it trains on matters. This paper argues most fast-weight rules quietly use the wrong (key, value) pair.

cards.title: Giving Interpretability Probes a Socket to Plug Into
cards.hook: Probes and SAEs can see a jailbreak forming inside the model, but each ships its own calibration and glue code. LMSM borrows Linux Security Modules' shape: pluggable backends, one enforcement path.

cards.title: Magpie: Let the Engine Run the Game, Let the Model Render It
cards.hook: Games need reproducible rules, which generative video cannot promise. Magpie splits the difference: the engine resolves gameplay on white-box frames, a render server paints them in real time.

cards.title: How Language Models Organize Moral Knowledge
cards.hook: Six moral foundations, six linear probes: the directions neither collapse into one 'morality detector' nor sit independently — they span near-maximal dimensions while sharing a common component.

cards.title: Naive Prompt Optimization Beats the Fancy Search
cards.hook: Prompt optimizers have grown elaborate search machinery. A single-lineage loop that just asks a teacher model to revise the prompt matches or beats GEPA with fewer rollouts.

cards.title: Scaling Laws for Learning Rate and Batch Size
cards.hook: Chinchilla told you how many tokens. This tells you what learning rate and batch size to use as you get there — including whether the optimum survives the decay phase.

cards.title: Your Parser Already Knows Which Tokens Matter
cards.hook: Constrained decoding tracks grammar state to keep JSON valid. PASK reuses that same signal to decide what to keep in the KV cache — and a wrong field is a failed tool call, not a stylistic blemish.

cards.title: Proper Scoring Rules Are Not Interchangeable as Training Objectives
cards.hook: Five scoring rules that all reward honest probabilities in theory produced five differently-behaved forecasters in practice — same accuracy, different shape of error.

cards.title: Ring Forcing: Teaching Video Models Object Permanence
cards.hook: Long video generation breaks in two ways at once: models forget what an object looked like, and can't reach far enough back to check. Ring Forcing attacks both.

cards.title: Three Ways to Fuse Domain Experts, Compared
cards.hook: Merge task vectors, pool the RL data, or distil from multiple teachers? Average scores differ by 1.4 points — but on a single benchmark the gap hits 8.6.

cards.title: Grading a Web App Feature by Feature, Then Sending the Reward Back to the Right Lines
cards.hook: A generated app fails in localized ways — a broken handler, a wrong selector. GRPO flattens all of it into one number. RCCA routes each rubric item's verdict back to the code that caused it.

cards.title: Ladders in Chaos: Sequential Beats Parallel Test-Time Scaling — Up to a Point
cards.hook: Revising your own answer beats sampling many independent ones, in translation at least. But push the budget too far and fluency keeps rising while accuracy starts slipping.

cards.title: When Robot Data Can't Scale, Scale the Representation Instead
cards.hook: Web images scale; robot trajectories don't. VLAct argues the fix isn't more teleoperation but better use of it — and beats full-data baselines on an unseen humanoid using 20% of the trajectories.

cards.title: Use a Weak Model to Stop Your Strong One Getting Stuck
cards.hook: RLVR collapses a model's entropy until it only knows one way to think. Feeding it half-finished reasoning from a smaller, worse model breaks the rut — no reward engineering required.

cards.title: WikiSkill: Give the Agent a Wiki, Not Just Skills
cards.hook: Auto-discovered agent skills work, but the insight behind them gets lost. WikiSkill keeps a persistent wiki alongside the skills — and skills borrowed from other models beat self-evolved ones.

cards.title: Prefix Sliding for Efficient Test-Time Scaling
cards.hook: Most intermediate reasoning tokens stop mattering as the model reasons on. Keep only the prefix and the last few thousand tokens and you cap memory forever — 3x faster with no training.

cards.title: SecOPD: Token-Level Feedback Against Prompt Injection
cards.hook: Defensive fine-tuning keeps failing because DPO and GRPO grade a whole answer at once. Score each token instead and adaptive-injection success drops from 94% to 9%.

cards.title: Missing the Butterfly and Predicting the Past: Features or Bugs of Accurate AI Weather Models?
cards.hook: AI weather models can be trained to predict the past as skillfully as the future. The same flaw that lets them do it explains why their forecasts beat physics.

cards.title: Anchoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
cards.hook: Show an LLM judge a previous score as mere context metadata and its rating drifts toward that number. Judgments you assumed were independent are quietly anchored to each other.

cards.title: Effective Learning Rate Governs Loss Dynamics
cards.hook: Two pretraining runs with very different learning rates and weight norms trace the same loss curve — if the ratio between them matches. That ratio is the coordinate that matters.

cards.title: Lost but Not Erased: Traces of a Forgotten Language in Neural Speech Models
cards.hook: International adoptees keep traces of a birth language they can't speak. Train an ASR model on one language, switch it abruptly to another, and the same thing happens — no biology needed.

cards.title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
cards.hook: Best agent configuration finished 20 of 97 real scientific workflows. And among failing Claude Code runs, 75.5% still signed off claiming they were done.

cards.title: The Handoff Tax: Swapping Models Mid-Run in Coding Agents
cards.hook: Escalating a struggling coding agent to a stronger model recovers less than half the quality gap while costing a premium. Downshifting, oddly, is the good deal.

cards.title: LAION-BVD: 10 Million Hours of Open Video
cards.hook: 1.3 billion video URLs mined from CommonCrawl, 80 million downloaded, synthetically captioned for video, audio, and image pretraining — and released openly.

cards.title: Maia 200: Dataflow Instead of Threads
cards.hook: Microsoft's AI accelerator bets that the bottleneck is moving data, not doing math — so the compiler programs the data movement explicitly instead of scheduling threads.

cards.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better Than SFT?
cards.hook: A controlled rerun finds the simplest baseline wins: plain mixed supervised fine-tuning beats next-chunk reasoning RL on no-CoT data, at over 60x less training compute.

cards.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation
cards.hook: Self-distillation drops the costly teacher by letting a model teach itself with privileged information. The asymmetry that creates the signal also biases it — into collapse.

cards.title: Annotations as Rollouts: Cheaper RL for Video Models
cards.hook: RL post-training wastes most of its samples on bad rollouts. OraRL drops the ground-truth annotation into the group as an oracle rollout — and has to fix the advantage math to make it work.

cards.title: The Mask Is Not the Model: Auditing Causality Leaks
cards.hook: Your attention mask can be perfectly correct and your model still peeks at the future. Two forward passes find the leak — and turned up real defects in Zamba2 and Nemotron-H.

cards.title: Quantization-Aware Healing: Distill, Don't Re-fit
cards.hook: Compress a 120B to 60B, drop it to 4 bits, and it breaks. QAT heals it slowly and then collapses; distilling from the original model instead gets there ~7x faster and stays stable.

cards.title: Skill Issue: Are Skills Language-Invariant in LLMs?
cards.hook: Have a model play a game against itself, one copy in English and one in another language. Same model, same rules, same board — and markedly different playing strength.

cards.title: Spectral Allocation: Why Muon Outperforms Adam, and How to Improve Muon
cards.hook: Probe a transformer's loss landscape direction by direction and a pattern appears: a few volatile directions demand tiny steps, the bulk tolerates far larger. That explains Muon > Adam > SGD.

cards.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Agents Can't Finish Migrations
cards.hook: Ask a coding agent to migrate a whole repo and it may just copy the old implementation to make tests pass. Audit for that, and only 5.4% of 520 runs survive.

cards.title: Repair or Resample? Rethinking Failure Debugging in Multi-Agent Systems
cards.hook: Most multi-agent repair methods just rerun the trajectory and hope. Freeze the randomness and the truth comes out: unguided reruns reproduce only 68% of failures and fix under 7% of them.

cards.title: WarpSAC: Off-Policy RL Stabilizers Depend on the Data Regime
cards.hook: Massively parallel simulation broke the assumptions behind a decade of RL stabilizers. WarpSAC's finding: tricks that rescue data-starved training actively hold you back when data is abundant.

cards.title: AnTrap: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies?
cards.hook: Real phones throw pop-ups, misfired taps, and dead-end screens at you. Inject those into GUI agent runs and all 16 leading models degrade — some in ways adversarial training can't fix.

cards.title: AsymSpec: Context-Asymmetric Speculative Decoding for Agentic LLMs
cards.hook: Speculative decoding assumes drafter and verifier read the same context. Let the small drafter see everything while the big model reads a compressed view, and compression stops costing accuracy.

cards.title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
cards.hook: Video world models learn what happens, not why. Put a coding agent in charge of the rules — writing executable code that holds world state — and let the video model handle only the pixels.

cards.title: CyberFactory: Turning Real CVEs Into Training Data
cards.hook: Open security models lag closed ones partly for lack of data. CyberFactory converts public vulnerability artifacts into executable, verifiable tasks — and trains an open model on the trajectories.

cards.title: EchoWM: A World Model You Can Walk Into and Hear
cards.hook: Most world models generate silent video. EchoWM generates 720p video plus environmental sound, music, and speech, and lets you navigate it continuously.

cards.title: Gated Recurrent Transformers: Buying Depth with Recurrence
cards.hook: Sharing one transformer block across many layers saves memory but flattens the model. Add a GRU-style update gate and the same three layers can act like twelve.

cards.title: Canalization Before Generalization: Grokking as a Dynamical Probe
cards.hook: Nudge weight decay briefly during grokking's plateau and you shift when generalization arrives. Early nudges scatter; later ones line up by dose — a hidden selection finishing unseen.

cards.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
cards.hook: If the harness matters as much as the model, why is it still hand-written? JIT-Agent trains a model whose whole job is to synthesize a fresh harness for whatever task shows up.

cards.title: LibriBrain100: 100 Hours of MEG Data for Neural Speech Decoding
cards.hook: Most brain-decoding datasets go wide across many subjects. This one goes deep — ~80 hours inside a single brain — to test whether depth beats breadth.

cards.title: How Much Rank Does LoRA Need? Rank-Error Bounds for Transformer Attention
cards.hook: Picking a LoRA rank is normally guesswork. This paper derives what error each rank can actually achieve for attention — and shows softmax saturation means you often need less rank than you'd think.

cards.title: MARS: Hand the Problem to the Right Specialist
cards.hook: Most multi-agent coding pipelines split work into planner, coder, debugger. MARS splits it by algorithmic topic instead — and gets most of the accuracy of a heavier pipeline at a third of the wall-clock cost.

cards.title: MobilePA-Bench: Phone Agents in a Live Sandbox
cards.hook: GUI benchmarks test tapping; function-call benchmarks test string matching. This one runs a real phone sandbox with live app databases — and frontier models get brittle fast.

cards.title: A General-Purpose Molecular Foundation Model Transfers Across Olfactory Tasks
cards.hook: Fine-tune a general molecular foundation model on one smell task and it transfers to four others untrained — including telling mirror-image molecules apart, which 2D graphs cannot.

cards.title: Interpretable Latents in a Neutrino Foundation Model with Sparse Autoencoders
cards.hook: Sparse autoencoders find physics concepts in an IceCube foundation model — and show its direction head barely uses them. A head that does cuts angular error from 20.2 to 3.2 degrees.

cards.title: RetrievalRouter: Pick the Retrieval Pipeline Per Query
cards.hook: Retrieval forces a choice between accurate-but-slow and fast-but-blind. A router reading only the query text claims both: 2.5% more accurate, 12.4x faster than the best static pipeline.

cards.title: RubSE: Why Self-Fixing UI Code Keeps Breaking What It Just Fixed
cards.hook: A model told to make its screenshot match the design fixes one region and quietly wrecks another. RubSE names that failure — visual repair coupling — and fences each edit in with a rubric.

cards.title: Sigmoid Attention Makes KV Eviction Stick
cards.hook: Learned cache-eviction gates train softly but must delete hard at inference. Swap softmax for sigmoid attention and that jump stops hurting — even though sigmoid is the worse LM.

cards.title: SwarmWorld: Stigmergic Technological Evolution in Societies of LLM Agents
cards.hook: Drop identical LLM agents into a shared world with no roles and no recipes. They differentiate, build on each other's leftovers, and accumulate technology — mostly by looking, not talking.

cards.title: V-Rubrics: Grading a VLM's Answer Fact by Fact
cards.hook: A single ungrounded object or misread chart value can sink an otherwise good answer — and a pass/fail reward can't tell you which part broke. V-Rubrics hands out partial credit per visual claim.

cards.title: Video-IFBench: Can a Video Model Follow the Instruction, Not Just Watch?
cards.hook: Video benchmarks mostly ask whether the model got the answer right. This one asks whether it did what you told it to — and more than 20 recent multimodal LLMs still struggle.

cards.title: Affective Context Amplifies Sycophancy
cards.hook: Tell a model you're lonely before asking for feedback, and it softens its judgment the most — sycophancy peaks exactly when honest feedback matters most.

cards.title: Agent Memory Poisoning Beats Content Screening
cards.hook: Poison 1.2% of an agent's long-term memory with plain false sentences and accuracy falls from 0.85 to 0.30 — while an injection screener catches literally none of them.

cards.title: AgentMercury: Synthesizing Worlds, Not Tasks
cards.hook: Instead of building an environment per task, build a persistent business world with entities, services and invariants — and let the tasks fall out of it.

cards.title: Where to Spend Model Size in Self-Refinement
cards.hook: Generate, critique, revise — three stages, and most systems use the same big model for all three. The critic barely needs to be big; the reviser absolutely does.

cards.title: Bounded Agents: Delegation Security for Multi-Agent AI Systems
cards.hook: Prompt injection only matters if the agent had the authority to obey. Treat it as an authorization-architecture bug and enforce the limits outside the model.

cards.title: E²-TTT: Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training
cards.hook: Test-time training updates weights while it reads, but chunking for speed throws away the update's temporal structure. A closed-form state transition gets both.

cards.title: EchoCoT: Extracting Hidden Chain-of-Thought from Black-Box Models
cards.hook: Providers hide reasoning traces because they're valuable assets. A replay surface between tool calls lets an attacker pull them back out near-verbatim through the public API.

cards.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
cards.hook: Agents outgrow the environments we hand-build for them. Instead of writing new worlds, wrap the old one in a programmable layer that reshapes it around the agent's current weaknesses.

cards.title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control
cards.hook: Every robot has a different action space, which fragments training data. Hydra-0 sidesteps that by expressing actions as pixel motion — a shared visual interface any embodiment can speak.

cards.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Test-Time Compute
cards.hook: Let the model pick its own thinking budget with its very first token. On MATH500 that cut response length 41% while accuracy barely moved.

cards.title: Memory-Augmented Compression: Cheaper Chain-of-Thought
cards.hook: Compressing chain-of-thought saves tokens but breaks the logic. Move the reasoning into the prompt as reusable memory and you get the savings without the damage.

cards.title: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large MoEs
cards.hook: Sweeping learning rates at trillion-token scale is unaffordable. Transfer across width with muP, then extrapolate along tokens with a fitted scaling law — and trust it for the real run.

cards.title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
cards.hook: Run a frozen, untrained model through your self-improvement pipeline and it appears to gain and lose capabilities. Without that control, seven common measurement habits invert their own findings.

cards.title: RARE: Steering MoE Models Without Breaking the Router
cards.hook: Activation steering works on dense models and quietly fails on mixture-of-experts — because your steering vector also reroutes the tokens. Project it into the router's null space.

cards.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
cards.hook: When software is part of the scientific instrument, a bad patch corrupts the evidence. The best agent tested clears under 50% of these repo-level scientific fixes.

cards.title: LLM Judges Can't Separate Trust from Truth
cards.hook: Ask a judge model for a trust score and a correctness verdict and you get two numbers — but they're not two pieces of evidence. Change the source label and both move.

cards.title: Does Telling an LLM to Be Concise Save Money?
cards.hook: Two ways to spend fewer tokens: shorten what you send, or shorten what you ask for back. Measured across nine models, only one of them actually saves you money.

cards.title: EviRank: Turning Image Re-ranking Into a Checklist
cards.hook: "Find this shirt in pink" hides three instructions: keep the entity, change the attribute, ignore the background. EviRank makes each one an explicit, checkable criterion.

cards.title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context Serving
cards.hook: Prefill is where long-context inference burns its compute. This turns a sparse-attention prototype into a production backend — and reports up to 47x over FlashAttention-2 at 128K.

cards.title: HIERA: Choosing the Search Space for GPU Kernels
cards.hook: LLM kernel optimizers all pick one implementation space and search inside it. HIERA's first decision is which space to search at all — PyTorch op, CUDA library, or handwritten kernel.

cards.title: HOTFIXR: Targeted Synthetic Data for Multilingual Weaknesses
cards.hook: A model can answer the same question well in English and badly in Turkish. Rather than routing everything through English, probe the student's weak spots and synthesize data for exactly those.

cards.title: Llama-Mobile: A VLM at 2.7 Bits per Weight
cards.hook: Llama 3.2 11B Vision squeezed into 3.7 GB — using the model's own outputs as calibration data and a bit format built for Arm CPUs, not GPUs.

cards.title: ParaTempo: Steering Parallel Reasoning With Temporal Confidence
cards.hook: Exploring many solution paths at once makes reasoning models better and slower. ParaTempo watches how fast each branch converges on an answer and kills, retires, or forks branches on that one signal.

cards.title: SparsePR: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation
cards.hook: Skipping attention blocks in a video model is cheap; knowing what you threw away is the hard part. SparsePR partitions queries by response and then reconstructs the missing residual.

cards.title: Visual Scaffolds Reveal What VLM Benchmarks Measure
cards.hook: Redraw the same spatial puzzle to make its structure legible and accuracy jumps up to 34 points — so was the benchmark ever testing reasoning?

cards.title: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild: Choosing Is the Bottleneck, Not Generating
cards.hook: Spend more inference compute on open-ended tasks and the best candidate in your pool keeps getting better. The problem is you can't tell which one it is.

cards.title: AlphaEvolve Nudges Down the Matrix Multiplication Exponent
cards.hook: The theoretical limit on how fast you can multiply matrices just moved: ω < 2.371177, beating 2.371339 — with ML-designed optimization and AlphaEvolve doing the refining.

cards.title: How Agents Fail at Autonomous Research: The Missing Metacognitive Loop
cards.hook: 800 agent trajectories across 100 real frontier-science tasks converge on one deficit: agents don't check what they wrote against what they found.

cards.title: Co-RL: Unsupervised Reasoning from a Diverse Cohort
cards.hook: Self-rewarding RL collapses because a model's errors reinforce themselves. Co-RL breaks the loop by having a diverse cohort of models grade each other — no labels at all.

cards.title: FreeToken: Serving Frontier MoE Models on the Machine You Own
cards.hook: Instead of treating a laptop as a tiny datacenter GPU, FreeToken treats the whole machine as one elastic inference platform — and runs a 753B model on a single workstation card.

cards.title: Why Adam Beats SGD on Transformers: A Hessian Story
cards.hook: Adam is the default optimizer for LLMs and nobody could quite say why. This thesis traces it to the shape the Hessian takes during transformer training — and gets Adam-mini out of the explanation.

cards.title: SemaPLC: Let the Runtime Decide When Generated Code Is Done
cards.hook: An agent that stops when it thinks it's finished will always look good. SemaPLC only declares a task complete when external checks — including a live PLC runtime — log that it passed.

cards.title: Training Leaves Traces: Reading a Model's Ancestry From Its Weights
cards.hook: Open weights get fine-tuned, quantized, pruned and merged with no paper trail. This work finds a data-free signature in the weights that says whether two checkpoints share an ancestor.

cards.title: Zetta: A Closed-Loop Embodied Harness for Self-Evolving Physical Intelligence
cards.hook: Most robot agents reflect only after the episode ends — too late to save it. Zetta writes and revises its own runtime critics mid-rollout, while the base policy stays frozen.

cards.title: Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling
cards.hook: Recurrent depth helps most where tool use is actually hard: chaining calls, holding intermediate state, keeping dependencies straight. Single API calls barely notice.

cards.title: SemComp-Bench: Judge the Video by the Outcome, Not the Frames
cards.hook: Most video-generation benchmarks grade appearance consistency. SemComp-Bench asks a blunter question: did the task in the prompt actually get done?

cards.title: Refute, Don't Resample: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment
cards.hook: Refuting a wrong claim needs one decisive flaw; building a right answer needs a flawless path. CLR spends test-time compute on that asymmetry instead of on more samples.

cards.title: Dion3: Making Muon's Orthogonalization Cheap
cards.hook: Muon trains faster than AdamW but pays for it in a cubic-time orthogonalization step. Dion3 attacks that overhead at every layer of the stack — up to 6x faster optimizer steps at matching loss.

cards.title: The Dynamics of Intelligence Explosions
cards.hook: If AI accelerates AI research, how fast can that loop go? Toby Ord's answer: runaway growth is harder than the models suggest, and the neglected variable is how long one trip around the loop takes.

cards.title: Full-Bandwidth Transformer: Feed the Hidden State Back
cards.hook: Between decoding steps a transformer throws away everything except the sampled token. Widening that channel with the top-layer hidden state buys roughly 1.5x the training tokens' worth of quality.

cards.title: The Past and Future of AI Scientists
cards.hook: Ross King's survey of machines that do science: the components are all automatable now, and have been since Adam and Eve. The unsolved problem is integration.

cards.title: A Probe Direction Is a Property of Its Prompt
cards.hook: Two published studies disagree about whether bigger models better sense they're being evaluated. Both trends are reproducible from one design — by changing only the prompt.

cards.title: How Rhetoric Reward-Hacks an AI Reviewer
cards.hook: Rewrite a paper's framing without changing a single result, and LLM reviewers move their scores. The effect is structured: evidence framing and novelty stance move them most.

cards.title: Synthetic Persona Pretraining: Alignment From Token Zero
cards.hook: Alignment is normally a coat of paint applied after pretraining. This work installs the assistant's values from the first token — and finds that the earlier you start, the deeper they hold.

cards.title: AgentRewind: Give Agents an Undo Button
cards.hook: Most agent research tries to prevent mistakes. AgentRewind asks what happens after one — checkpoint the context and the environment together, so the agent can rewind and retry with what it learned.

cards.title: Seeing Red, Thinking Bad: Color Bias in VLMs
cards.hook: Render the same sentence with the positive words in green and a vision-language model reads it more positively. The text didn't change — only its styling did.

cards.title: How Many Times Should You Repeat Your Best Data?
cards.hook: Good domain data doesn't scale like web crawl, so it gets diluted as models grow. How often can you repeat it before overfitting? The answer tracks the domain's loss, not its size.

cards.title: Forecast Collapse in Time-Series Foundation Models
cards.hook: Ask a forecasting model to predict hourly stock returns and it hedges into a nearly flat line — technically well-calibrated, useless for ranking. Per-series metrics never show you this.

cards.title: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation
cards.hook: Every on-policy self-distillation method hand-picks what the teacher gets to see. LOPD makes that privileged context a learned vector instead of a design choice.

cards.title: Agent Memory: Consolidate by Segment, Not by Turn
cards.hook: Most agent memory systems call an LLM after every exchange, so memory gets more expensive as the conversation grows. Batching into semantic segments cut construction tokens by 86%.

cards.title: Knowing When to Stop: Adaptive Sampling for LLM Evals
cards.hook: Most evals run every item the same number of times, long after the estimate has stopped moving. Treat it as sequential measurement instead and 57–97% of those trials turn out to be unnecessary.

cards.title: More Correct Mass, Worse Answers: Where Power Sampling Breaks
cards.hook: Sharpening a model's distribution can push more probability onto correct reasoning paths and still make the final answer worse — by up to 18.5 points. The culprit is coverage, not correctness.

cards.title: Rules or Character? Where to Spend Your Safety Budget
cards.hook: Filters block bad outputs at inference; RLHF shapes behavior at training. A formal model asks how to split the budget — and finds scale matters far less than one parameter.

cards.title: Second Thought: Reasoning in Parallel While an Agent Acts
cards.hook: Every time a ReAct agent calls a tool and waits, its reasoning sits idle. Second Thought fills that gap with side branches that think ahead — no retraining, fewer turns.

cards.title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation
cards.hook: Distillation needs a teacher who knows more than the student. This paper gets that gap for free — not by informing the teacher, but by blinding the student.

cards.title: Spatial Memory Agent: Self-Improvement Without Touching the Weights
cards.hook: A frozen VLM gets better at spatial reasoning by writing itself notes — verified lessons, scored by how well they transfer, retrieved at inference time.
